Surface: backend

Origin: ledger resolve gate (#4368 review lens 3e, tiebreak-confirmed, ledger item 11)

**Related:** #4501, #4531, #4283, #4350, #4351, #4577

## Current State

Two modules read a record's `Origin:` line, and each takes the **first** line matching `^Origin:` anywhere in the body:

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/provenance.js` (`ORIGIN_LINE`, `:35`) classifies the record's side-effect trust class.
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/trust.js` (`ORIGIN_LINE_RE`, `:79`, read by `correctiveFollowUpTarget`) counts a `from #N` corrective follow-up against the named record's class.

Neither skips fenced code blocks, which #4368 made the executor-facing extractors do (`record-payload.js`'s `fencedLineMask`/`unfencedText`). Neither skips text quoted from another record either.

A real-data audit over all 2,847 records on 2026-10-30 found:

- **No fenced `Origin:` line anywhere.** Making the readers fence-aware changes no record's provenance today.
- **The record's own `Origin:` line sits in three places:**
  - at the top of the body (918 records);
  - under `## Original request` (170 records) — specify's shaping mode moves the original stub there, and for those records it is the only `Origin:` line;
  - under another section of an older template (36 records), each of them that record's own line.
- **Another record's `Origin:` line appears only under `## Absorbed: …` headings,** which `/claude-tweaks:capture`'s absorb route appends (`plugin/skills/capture/routing.md`). In all 10 records that carry one, the record's own line comes first, so first-match has never misread a record.

**The latent hazard:** a human-filed record has no `Origin:` line of its own. If it absorbs a capture whose text carries one, first-match reads the absorbed line, and the record moves from `human:human` to that capture's side-effect class. If the absorbed text names `from #N`, `trust.js` also counts a corrective follow-up against #N's class. Capture's absorb route can create this at any time.

`plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-fingerprint.js` was named in the original request, but it never reads `Origin:`. Its `work-fingerprint` markers are already defused when quoted text is composed (`defuse`, `:55`), so it is out of scope.

**Decision (human-approved 2026-10-30):** a record's provenance comes from its **own** `Origin:` line only:

- a line inside a fenced code block never counts;
- a line under a `## Absorbed: …` heading never counts;
- a line under `## Original request` still counts, because it is the record's own earlier text.

## Deliverables

1. Add `ownOriginLine(body)` to `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-payload.js`, beside `fencedLineMask`/`unfencedText`. It:
   - returns the text after `Origin:` on the first line matching `^Origin:` that is neither inside a fenced block (per `fencedLineMask`) nor inside a `## Absorbed:` section;
   - treats an `## Absorbed:` section as running from its heading to the next line starting `## `;
   - returns `null` when no such line exists;
   - splits lines exactly as `unfencedText` does (CRLF, lone CR, LF).
2. `provenance.js` reads the line through `ownOriginLine` instead of `ORIGIN_LINE.exec(body)`. The capture semantics stay the same: a bare `Origin:` still resolves to `unstructured:empty-origin`, and the over-length and `TRAILING_SOURCE` handling is unchanged.
3. `trust.js`'s `correctiveFollowUpTarget` reads the same line through `ownOriginLine`, so the class and the follow-up count can never come from different lines.
4. Update the "Still fence-blind" note in `record-payload.js` (`:34`), and the readers' header comments, to state the rule.
5. Tests, in the existing suites for `provenance.js`, `trust.js` and `record-payload.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A body with no top `Origin:` line and an `## Absorbed: 2026-10-30 — x` section holding `Origin: demo changes-requested from #7` resolves to `human:human`. In a `trustRows` fixture it adds no follow-up to #7's class.
- A body whose only `Origin:` line is inside a fenced block (backtick and tilde fence) resolves to `human:human`.
- A body whose only `Origin:` line is under `## Original request` resolves to that line's class, as today.
- A body with an own top line and an absorbed section still resolves to the top line's class.
- A line after the absorbed section's next `## ` heading counts again.
- A bare `Origin:` still yields `unstructured:empty-origin`.
- CRLF bodies resolve the same as LF bodies.
- Each new rule has a test that goes red when the rule is reverted. Revert the Absorbed skip, then the fence skip, and show which test fails for each.
- The PR re-runs the 2026-10-30 audit: `resolveProvenance` over every record before and after, across all states. It reports the number of records whose result changed, which is expected to be 0, and names any that did.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Trust tracking no longer takes a record's origin from text quoted out of another record.

## Technical Approach

One shared helper, so the two readers cannot drift apart again. The helper lives in `record-payload.js` because that module already owns the fence rule and the body-metadata line conventions (`Defer-reason:`, `Verified-as-of:`). It reuses `fencedLineMask` rather than a second fence scanner. A section boundary is a line starting `## `; only `## Absorbed:` sections are skipped.

The audit script for the last acceptance row reads records with `gh issue list --state all --json number,body,labels` and calls `resolveProvenance` on each body, once from `main` and once from the branch.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-payload.js` — add and export `ownOriginLine`; update the fence-blind note
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/provenance.js` — read through `ownOriginLine`
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/trust.js` — `correctiveFollowUpTarget` reads through `ownOriginLine`
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/provenance.test.js` — new `resolveProvenance` cases
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/trust.test.js` — new follow-up cases, through `trustRows` (`correctiveFollowUpTarget` is internal, not exported)
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/record.test.js` — `ownOriginLine` unit cases, beside the existing `fencedLineMask`/`unfencedText` cases

## Gotchas

- `## Original request` must keep counting. For 170 records it holds the only `Origin:` line, and skipping it would silently reclassify all of them as human.
- `record-fingerprint.js` is out of scope (see Current State). Don't widen this change to it.
- The issue author is not checked: an outsider filing an issue in a public consumer repo can write any `Origin:` line at the top. That is #4577, not this record.
- `record-payload.js` must not require `provenance.js` or `trust.js`. The dependency runs the other way.

## Original request

Decide whether a quoted Origin: line may set a record's provenance

Origin: ledger resolve gate (#4368 review lens 3e, tiebreak-confirmed, ledger item 11)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

#4368 made the Premise-check, Verified-as-of and Template extractors skip lines inside fenced code blocks, because those feed the shell executor in `materialize.js`. The `Origin:` readers (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/provenance.js`, `plugin/bin/lib/issues/trust.js`) and the work-fingerprint reader (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-fingerprint.js`) stay fence-blind, so an `Origin:` line quoted inside a fenced block can still be read as the record's provenance. None of them feeds a shell executor, so #4368 left them unchanged. Whether a quoted `Origin:` line should count is a trust-semantics call on files that diff did not touch.

**Related:** #4501, #4531

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide the policy for a quoted `Origin:` line, then apply it to `provenance.js`, `trust.js` and `record-fingerprint.js` as one change with tests, or record the decision to leave them fence-blind.

## Open Question

Should an `Origin:` line inside a fenced block count as the record's provenance, or must provenance readers skip fenced lines the way the executor-facing extractors now do?

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

Origin: ledger resolve gate (#4368 review lens 3b, tiebreak-confirmed, ledger item 10)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-payload.js`'s shared fence rule (`fencedLineRanges`/`unfencedText`, widened by #4368 to 0-3 space indentation, backtick/tilde fences, BOM and CRLF) pairs openers and closers by scanning lines in order. It is not container-aware: an indented fence opened inside a list item, and fence-looking lines inside a raw HTML block, shift the pairing, so a `Premise-check:` line that GitHub renders inside a code block can be read and run by `materialize.js`. Reaching it needs a trusted author writing unbalanced Markdown, who can already write an unfenced command line, so the exposure is low. #4368 left it because a correct fix tracks list-item and HTML-block containers across every consumer of the shared rule (the three extractors, `recordPayload`'s Defer-reason check, and `stripCodeSpans` in `materialize-format.js`).

**Related:** #4502, #4531

## Deliverables

- [ ] Track list-item and raw-HTML-block containers in the shared fence rule so an opener or closer is paired only within its own container, as CommonMark and GitHub do.
- [ ] Update every consumer of the shared rule to use it (no second copy of the pairing logic).
- [ ] Add tests in `tests/bin-lib/issues/record.test.js` for a fence opened in a list item and for fence-looking lines in a raw HTML block, each followed by a quoted `Premise-check:` line.

## Acceptance Criteria

`extractPremiseCheck` returns `null` for a body whose only `Premise-check:` line sits inside a fence opened in a list item, and for one that follows fence-looking lines in a raw HTML block; the new tests fail when the container tracking is reverted.

## Release Note

Fix: a quoted Premise-check line inside a fenced block opened in a list item, or after fence-looking lines in a raw HTML block, is no longer read as the record's command.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-payload.js` — container-aware pairing in the shared fence rule
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/record.test.js` — list-item and HTML-block fence cases

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3976, #3721, #3974, #3975, #4244, #4330, #4368, #4387, #4492, #4501, #4502

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:flow`'s materialize step (`plugin/bin/materialize.js`, `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md`) writes the record to `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run}/work/{n}-spec.md` and commits it. That file is the run's tracked audit trail (`materialize.md:185`). The rest of the run dir stays ignored, and the committable `work/` children are re-included level by level, because a blanket ignore on a parent directory makes nested `!` re-inclusion impossible.

`/claude-tweaks:init` Step 4 (`plugin/skills/init/bootstrap/step-04-gitignore-suggestions.md`) suggests the split ignore block (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/*`, `!.claude-tweaks/pipelines/*/`, `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/*/*`, plus the `work/` carve-outs at `:14-27`). On re-run it migrates an old standalone blanket `.claude-tweaks/` line. This repo's own `.gitignore:12-33` carries the carve-outs. Nothing outside init checks for them: `materialize.js` has no `git check-ignore` call.

Observed on 6.156.1: a project whose `.gitignore` ignores the whole `.claude-tweaks/` directory had never re-run init. Flow's plain `git add` of `work/{n}-spec.md` was refused, so the build force-added it. That left the only tracked file under an ignored directory, shipped with the branch (in a template repo, to every clone), and forced a keep-or-untrack decision at merge time. The workaround was the force-add plus a ledger item.

## Deliverables

1. In `materialize.js`, before committing, run `git check-ignore -q` on the target spec path. When it is ignored, never force-add. Exit with a named, non-zero outcome whose message says the spec path is gitignored, that `/claude-tweaks:init` migrates a blanket `.claude-tweaks/` ignore to the split form, and shows the minimal carve-out lines from `step-04-gitignore-suggestions.md:14-19`.
2. Add the same check to flow's preflight (`plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js`), so the problem surfaces at the Pipeline Config Manifesto before any work starts, not at materialize. Report it as a preflight finding naming the fix command.
3. In `auto` mode the run proceeds without stopping. Materialize writes the spec untracked, never force-added. The run stages a `.gitignore` carve-out patch (per `_shared/staged-patch.md`, generated from a real `git diff` of the edited `.gitignore`) and logs a `STAGED` decision line naming it, so the Review Console offers the fix. A new mid-flow stop is not used: the auto-mode contract's HARD-GATE list is closed, and adding one is a contract change this record does not make. Interactive modes ask once at preflight instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a fixture repo whose `.gitignore` contains a blanket `.claude-tweaks/` line, `materialize.js` exits with the new named outcome and the message names `/claude-tweaks:init`. No file is force-added (`git ls-files .claude-tweaks` is empty afterwards).
- With init's split ignore block in place, materialize commits the spec exactly as today.
- Flow preflight on the blanket-ignore fixture reports the finding before the Manifesto.
- In `auto` mode on the blanket-ignore fixture, the run does not stop. `staged/` holds a `.gitignore` carve-out patch that passes `git apply --check`, and `decisions.md` carries a `STAGED` line naming it.

## Release Note

Pipelines now detect a `.gitignore` that hides the committed spec file and point to `/claude-tweaks:init` to fix it, instead of force-adding a stray tracked file.

## Technical Approach

The reporter offered three fixes: detect at materialize/init and offer the carve-out, document the carve-out as a prerequisite and check it in pre-flight, or move the committed spec to a path outside plugin state. Detection plus the existing init migration is chosen. Init already owns the canonical ignore block and its blanket-line migration, so detection only needs to route there. Relocating the spec would break every reader that resolves `work/{n}-spec.md` under the run dir: `flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`, archive-run, and reconcile's work/ handling. That is out of proportion to a `.gitignore` fix.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/materialize.js` — check-ignore guard and named outcome
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` — preflight finding
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — document the guard and the auto-mode choice
- `plugin/skills/init/bootstrap/step-04-gitignore-suggestions.md` — reference: canonical carve-out block and migration

## Gotchas

- `git check-ignore` exits 1 for "not ignored" and 128 on error. Only exit 0 means ignored, and an error is not "not ignored": surface it.
- Multi-spec runs materialize under `spec-{n}/work/`. Check the actual target path, not a fixed pattern.
- The preflight finding must respect the auto-mode contract's two-stop rule. In `auto` it is shown in the Manifesto FYI and staged, never a stop.

## Original request

materialize: committing work/{n}-spec.md needs a force-add when the project gitignores .claude-tweaks/

**Summary:** When a project gitignores `.claude-tweaks/`, flow's materialized `work/{n}-spec.md` can only be committed with a force-add, leaving the only tracked file under an ignored directory.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `bin/materialize.js` / flow Step 4 (materialize-and-commit `work/{n}-spec.md`)

**Use case:** The project's `.gitignore` ignores the whole `.claude-tweaks/` directory, which is a common choice because it holds pipeline run state. Flow materializes the record to `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run}/work/{n}-spec.md` and expects to commit it. A plain `git add` is refused for an ignored path, so the build had to force-add it. That left the only tracked file under an otherwise-ignored directory. The file then ships with the branch, and in a template repo with every project cloned from it. A human had to decide at merge time whether to keep it.

What would help, any one of:
- materialize (or `/claude-tweaks:init`) detects that the target path is ignored and offers the minimal carve-out (`!.claude-tweaks/pipelines/*/work/`), or
- the plugin documents that carve-out as a prerequisite and checks it in pre-flight, or
- the committed spec lives at a path that isn't plugin-state (e.g. `docs/` or `work/` at the repo root), configurable via policy.

**Why it matters:** the plugin relies on the committed spec for its audit trail. When the project gitignores `.claude-tweaks/`, that trail either needs a force-add, which leaves a stray tracked file, or is lost.

**Workaround used:** force-adding the spec, with a ledger item asking the human to keep it (and add a carve-out) or untrack it before merge.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.156.1

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #4494, #4499, #3256, #3396, #3721, #3813, #3822, #3875, #3878, #3975, #3982, #3995, #4275, #4360, #4362, #4366, #4442, #4452

## Current State

Policy reads anchor `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` to the current checkout's root. `resolvePolicyConfig` (`plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js:692-703`) takes `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (cwd fallback) and joins the path onto it. `readPolicyFile(repoRoot)` (`plugin/bin/lib/policy.js:15`) and `auditPolicy(repoRoot)` (`policy-schema.js`) do the same with a caller-supplied root. 14 `plugin/bin` modules read policy through these, among them `pr-early-open.js`, `resolve-policy.js`, `hooks/pre-tool-use.js`, `flow/preflight.js`, `release-preflight/pack.js`, `wrap-up/pack.js` and `express/policy.js`.

When a project gitignores `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` (or all of `.claude-tweaks/`), a fresh linked worktree has no copy. From a worktree cwd every key then reads as unset, silently. The run's `{runDir}/config.yml` overlay does not carry `integration-branch` either.

Three independent reports on 6.156.1 (this record, #4494, #4499) hit the same failure. The main checkout's policy set `integration-branch: develop`, GitHub's default branch was `main`, and `/claude-tweaks:flow #N` ran with the worktree strategy under `pr-first`. Flow's Step 2.5 divergence check, run from the main checkout, resolved `develop`. `/claude-tweaks:build` then ran `pr-early-open.js` from inside the worktree. There the key was unset, the integration-branch ladder (`_shared/integration-branch.md`) fell through to `defaultBranchRef`, and the draft PR opened against `main`. Each operator retargeted by hand with `gh pr edit --base develop`. One copied `policy.yml` into the worktree so later phases resolved `develop`. A run nobody watched would have built, reviewed and merge-gated against the production branch. The same blind spot applies to every worktree-side policy read (`worktree-always`, timeouts, `port-services`, …), not only `integration-branch`.

`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/` already solves this for the run directory: `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s Anchoring section resolves `$RUN_ROOT` to the main checkout through `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`.

## Deliverables

1. One policy-file locator used by `resolvePolicyConfig`, `readPolicyFile` and `auditPolicy`. If `<root>/.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` exists, read it, so a tracked, branch-local policy keeps today's behavior. If it is absent and `root` is a linked worktree, read the main checkout's `policy.yml` instead (the parent of `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, resolved the same way as `$RUN_ROOT`).
2. Return which file was read (worktree or main checkout) from `resolvePolicyConfig`. `resolve-policy.js` emits a one-line stderr degrade note when the main-checkout fallback was used.
3. `pr-early-open.js` warns on stderr whenever it falls back to the GitHub default branch while running in a linked worktree, naming both the resolved base and the fact that no `integration-branch` was found.
4. The fix PR closes this record, #4494 and #4499 with closing keywords. All three report this one defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- From a linked worktree whose project gitignores `.claude-tweaks/`, with `integration-branch: develop` in the main checkout's policy, `resolve-policy.js --values integration-branch` prints `develop` and `pr-early-open.js` resolves base `develop`.
- When the worktree has its own tracked `policy.yml`, that file wins: the main checkout's is not read.
- From the main checkout, behavior is byte-identical to today.
- `pr-early-open.js` run from a linked worktree with no `integration-branch` anywhere prints the fallback warning and still opens against the default branch.
- Unit tests cover the three locator cases (worktree file present, worktree absent with main present, both absent), using a fake `git` runner as `blast-radius-cli.js`'s tests already do. One end-to-end test runs `resolve-policy.js` in a real temporary linked worktree.

## Release Note

Pipelines running in a worktree now read the main checkout's `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` when the project keeps that file out of git, so draft PRs target the configured integration branch instead of the GitHub default.

## Technical Approach

The reporters offered three fixes: fall back to the main checkout's policy, copy `integration-branch` into the run's `config.yml` at the Manifesto, or have `pr-early-open.js` refuse a base that differs from the manifest's. The fallback is chosen because it fixes every policy key and every reader at once, in the one place they share. The other two fix only `integration-branch`, and only for runs that went through the Manifesto. Reuse the existing `$RUN_ROOT` resolution (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`, and the helper the hooks already use to find the main checkout) rather than writing a second `--git-common-dir` parser.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js` — `resolvePolicyConfig` and `auditPolicy` use the locator
- `plugin/bin/lib/policy.js` — `readPolicyFile` uses the locator
- `plugin/bin/resolve-policy.js` — degrade note when the fallback was used
- `plugin/bin/pr-early-open.js` — default-branch fallback warning in a worktree
- `plugin/skills/_shared/integration-branch.md` — rank 3 reads policy through the locator; note the worktree fallback
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` — reference: the existing main-checkout anchoring

## Gotchas

- `hooks/pre-tool-use.js` reads policy on the hook hot path (the `worktree-always` gate). The fallback adds at most one `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` call and one file stat. Keep it lazy, only when the worktree file is absent, and check `perf/` budgets.
- A worktree cwd that is not inside any git repo must keep the current `process.cwd()` fallback, not throw.
- On Windows, `--git-common-dir` can return a relative or forward-slash path. Resolve it against the cwd before taking its parent.

## Original request

policy resolution in worktrees: gitignored policy.yml is invisible, so pr-early-open targets the default branch

**Summary:** A gitignored `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` in the main checkout is invisible inside a `/flow` worktree, so `pr-early-open.js` opens the draft PR against the default branch instead of the configured `integration-branch`.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** policy resolution in linked worktrees (`bin/resolve-policy.js`, as consumed by `bin/pr-early-open.js` from `/claude-tweaks:build` Spec Step 1)

**Repro steps:**
1. In a repo whose default branch is `main` but whose PRs target `develop`, put `integration-branch: develop` in the gitignored `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` of the main checkout.
2. Run `/claude-tweaks:flow #N` (default `worktree` strategy, `integration-model: pr-first`).
3. Flow's Step 2.5 divergence check, run from the main checkout, resolves `develop` correctly.
4. `/build` creates the worktree with `EnterWorktree` and runs `bin/pr-early-open.js` from inside it after the materialize commit.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the draft PR targets `develop`, the configured integration branch.
Actual: inside the worktree, `resolve-policy.js --values integration-branch` prints nothing. The worktree's own `.claude-tweaks/` holds only `pipelines/`, because the gitignored `policy.yml` is never copied into a new worktree. So `pr-early-open.js` opens the draft PR against `main`, the production branch. It was caught by eye and retargeted by hand (`gh pr edit --base develop`). One run therefore used two different integration branches: the main-checkout readers saw `develop`, and every worktree-side reader saw the default branch.

**Suggested fix:** resolve `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` the same way the run directory is already anchored (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s Anchoring section). From a linked worktree, fall back to the main checkout's `policy.yml` when the worktree has none (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, then its parent). Alternatively, have `pr-early-open.js` refuse to open the PR when the integration branch it resolved differs from the one the run's manifest recorded.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.156.1

## Current State

#4420 routed `checkResumeFreshness` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js`) and `parentLiveDetail` (`plugin/bin/lib/flow/consolidated-pass.js`) through run-liveness via the shared `blocksResume`/`resumeEntries` helpers, but the extraction stopped halfway:

- **The resume ladder is hand-copied in both callers.** Lock positive → commit positive → `blocksResume` → `no-commits` → indeterminate, including the identical `(lock.result !== 'negative' ? lock : commit).detail` pick, at `resume-freshness.js:86-102` and `consolidated-pass.js:59-66`. `run-liveness/index.js`'s `blocksResume` comment says `no-commits` does not block because both callers handle it themselves, so the fail-closed `no-commits` rung lives in two copies kept in sync only by prose. No test asserts the two ladders agree: `tests/bin-lib/flow/consolidated-pass.test.js` stubs `checkResumeFreshness`.
- **`checkResumeFreshness` side-channels the commit time.** The `last-commit` evidence entry carries only `{result, detail}`, so `resume-freshness.js:83-85` wraps the probe in a closure that assigns an outer `commitAt` to compute `ageMs`. That only holds while `runLiveness` calls the injected probe exactly once and synchronously. If the default probe ran instead, `commitAt` would stay `null` and `ageMs` would silently read as `now`.

Found by the v6.156.2 release-gate whole-branch review (lens 3e, reproduced by both agents; cross-lens debate converged at medium; the consolidated-pass duplication separately tiebreak-confirmed). The release reviewed already-merged history, so it filed this rather than fixing it. `Premise-check:` exits 0 while the side channel is still present.

## Deliverables

- `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/index.js`: one resume-verdict helper (e.g. `resumeVerdict(result)` → `{ kind: 'locked' | 'recent-commit' | 'indeterminate' | 'clear', entry, commitAgeMs }`) that owns the whole ladder, `no-commits` rung included. The `last-commit` evidence entry carries the commit time or age, so callers need no side channel.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js` and `plugin/bin/lib/flow/consolidated-pass.js`: each maps that verdict to its own output shape (`{safe, verdict, reason, ageMs}` / detail string), keeping its own pre-probe status gates.
- One test that feeds the same evidence (lock error, commit error, `no-commits`, lock positive, commit positive, all negative) through both callers and asserts their verdict kinds agree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git grep -n -F "commitAt = lastCommitAt" -- plugin/bin` prints nothing (it matches `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js:85` at 05dc74c).
- [ ] `git grep -n -F "(lock.result !== 'negative' ? lock : commit).detail" -- plugin/bin` prints nothing outside `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/` (it matches `consolidated-pass.js:63` and `resume-freshness.js:100` at 05dc74c).
- [ ] The agreement test above fails when the `no-commits` rung is removed from either caller's mapping and passes with both intact.
- [ ] Existing `tests/hooks-resume-freshness.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/flow/consolidated-pass.test.js` and `tests/run-liveness-callers-conformance.test.js` pass unchanged in behavior.

## Release Note

No user-visible change. Interrupted-run resume checks and the multi-spec consolidated-pass banner now share one fail-closed decision path.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/index.js` — add the shared resume-verdict helper; carry commit age on the last-commit evidence entry
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js` — map the shared verdict; drop the commitAt closure
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/consolidated-pass.js` — map the shared verdict instead of re-implementing the ladder
- `tests/run-liveness-callers-conformance.test.js` — or a new suite: assert both callers agree on the same evidence

## Current State

After a full reconcile pass on 2026-10-27, `archive-branches` still skipped 97 local branches as `merged-pr-without-cherry-equivalence`, and `remote-prune` skipped 93 remote branches as `not-proven-merged`. Checking the 97 by hand: 62 had a tip exactly equal to their merged PR's `headRefOid`, 28 had a tip that was an ancestor of it, and only 7 carried commits made after the merge. The 90 contained ones were deleted by hand during the tidy close-out. The 7 were tag-archived (`archive/{branch}`) and deleted, matching archive-branches' unmerged-aged treatment.

## Deliverables

Approach: Add the PR-head containment proof next to cherry-equivalence and squash provenance: a MERGED PR whose `headRefOid` equals the branch tip, or has the tip as an ancestor, proves nothing on the branch is unmerged; the commits stay recoverable at `refs/pull/N/head`.

1. Add a PR-head containment proof (tip equal to, or ancestor of, the merged PR's head) to both checks' merged-in-substance evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A branch whose tip equals its merged PR's head is deleted by `archive-branches` (local) and `remote-prune` (remote).

## Release Note

reconcile now cleans up merged branches whose history includes merge commits or several squashed commits.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-branches.js` — merged proof
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/prune-remote.js` — merged proof
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/squash-provenance.js` — neighbouring proof to extend or reuse

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (base-branch requirement): Reading B — the PR-head containment proof holds only when the confirmed per-branch PR is MERGED, its `baseRefName` equals the bare integration branch name, and its `headRefOid` equals the branch tip or has the tip as an ancestor. A MERGED PR into any other base (a stacked PR) proves nothing, and both checks keep skipping it. `PR_LIST_ARGS` (`pr-state.js`) must add `headRefOid` and `baseRefName`. AC amended to: "A branch whose tip equals the head of its PR merged into the integration branch is deleted by `archive-branches` (local) and `remote-prune` (remote); a branch whose tip equals the head of a PR merged into a non-integration base is not."
- Q2 (post-merge commits): Reading A — out of scope. A MERGED-PR branch that fails cherry-equivalence, squash provenance and PR-head containment (that is, it gained commits after the merge) keeps skipping as `merged-pr-without-cherry-equivalence` on every pass. `decideArchive`'s age rules (`BRANCH_AGE_DAYS` tag-and-delete) still apply only to no-PR and CLOSED-unmerged branches, and `remote-prune` is unchanged.

## Current State

`classifyMirror` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/classify.js`, main) returns `dirty` whenever `git status --porcelain` prints anything, untracked files included, and `mirror-ff.js` then skips the fast-forward. A 2-byte stray file `f` in the main checkout kept the mirror un-synced for more than a day (2026-10-25 to 2026-10-27).

## Deliverables

Approach: Classify the mirror by what a fast-forward would actually touch: tracked modifications block it; untracked files block it only when they collide with a path the incoming range adds (`git merge --ff-only` already refuses that case safely). For tidy, write the post-commit log lines (PR opened, arm outcome) into the committed trail before the commit, or keep them out of the un-ignored files.

1. Narrow the dirty classification so an untracked file that does not collide with the incoming range no longer blocks the fast-forward.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An untracked file at a path the incoming range does not touch no longer stops reconcile's mirror fast-forward.

## Release Note

reconcile keeps the main checkout in sync even when it holds unrelated untracked files, including tidy's own run trail.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/classify.js` — mirror dirty classification
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/mirror-ff.js` — fast-forward gate
- `plugin/skills/tidy/step-7-5-worktree-always.md` — log-before-commit ordering

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (tidy trail collides with incoming range): Reading A — keep the Release Note and Approach. Beyond Deliverable 1, a colliding untracked file stops blocking the mirror fast-forward when its bytes equal the incoming blob at that path (`git hash-object <file>` == `git rev-parse origin/{integration}:<path>`). Reconcile removes such files immediately before `git merge --ff-only`, re-hashing each one just before unlinking it, and restores them from the blob if the merge then fails. Any colliding file whose content differs, or whose hash cannot be read, keeps the mirror `dirty` and nothing is removed (fail closed). `plugin/skills/tidy/step-7-5-worktree-always.md` keeps its post-commit lines (PR opened, arm outcome) out of the committed trail files, so the main-checkout copies stay byte-identical. It also drops its incorrect claim that committing only the worktree copies avoids a later `git pull` refusal. Added AC: a tidy/sweep-standalone run dir whose untracked `decisions.md`/`report.md`/`staged/**` match the merged housekeeping PR's copies byte for byte no longer stops the fast-forward; a colliding untracked file with different content still does.

## Current State

`resolvePrStatesBulk` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js`, line 385 on main) returns `network-failure` for the WHOLE screen when any single branch's `associatedPullRequests(first:10)` page has `hasNextPage`. On 2026-10-27 the local branch `worktree-sweep` (a reused session branch name, 15 merged PRs) did exactly that: every one of 441 in-scope branches reported `skip:network-failure` in `archive-branches`, and `remote-prune` reported `pr-screen-failed`. GitHub rate limits were fine and every GraphQL chunk returned exit 0 in about 1.5 s.

## Deliverables

Approach: Bound the failure to the branch that caused it: a truncated `associatedPullRequests` page puts that branch on a per-branch fallback (the REST `pr list --head` resolver), and the rest of the chunk keeps its screened state. Distinguish the reason from a transport failure in the result vocabulary.

1. Resolve a truncated-page branch individually (per-branch confirm) instead of failing the chunk, keeping the module's "never a silent partial" posture for genuinely incomplete responses (missing alias, GraphQL errors).

## Acceptance Criteria

- With one branch having more than 10 associated PRs, `archive-branches` and `remote-prune` still classify every other branch in the same pass (test fixture).

## Release Note

reconcile no longer stops cleaning up branches repo-wide because one branch name was reused across many PRs.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js` — resolvePrStatesBulk truncated-page handling
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-branches.js` — consume the per-branch result
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/prune-remote.js` — same, and its pr-screen-failed path

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (capped fallback): Reading B, closed in this record. Under `preferOpen`, a truncated `associatedPullRequests` page that already shows an OPEN node resolves to that OPEN PR with no fallback. Otherwise a truncated branch goes to the per-branch `gh pr list --head` fallback, which passes an explicit `--limit`. A fallback (or prune-remote's per-branch confirm of that branch) whose row count reaches that limit counts as incomplete: that branch fails closed (skip), never a decision. Every other branch keeps its screened state.
- Q2 (result vocabulary): Reading B — the distinction must reach the checks' observable output. In `archive-branches` and `remote-prune`, a branch whose PR page was truncated and that ends as a skip reports a distinct entry reason, never bare `network-failure`. Use `pr-page-truncated` when its fallback hit the row limit (Q1), and `pr-page-truncated:network-failure` / `pr-page-truncated:gh-absent` when the fallback call itself failed. A truncated branch whose fallback resolved cleanly is classified and reported normally. The bulk screen's internal return value may carry its own sentinel.

## Current State

Both shapes fail open at base d9aa6b82d, at main's #4281 and at the merged #4303 head 1b7caaca8. Checked with `fileWriteTargets` from cwd `/r`.

- `echo x > '(x'` resolves no target, but bash 3.2 and 5 write the file `/r/(x`. The redirect scan skips a target that starts with `(`, so that it never reads a process substitution as a file, and it does this even when the `(` is quoted.
- `cd>f /main; cp a g.js` resolves `/r/f` and `/r/g.js`. Bash writes `f` in `/r`, changes to `/main`, and writes `/main/g.js`. The cd walk reads the lead word `cd>f` as no `cd` at all, because the redirect is glued to the builtin name.

## Deliverables

1. Skip a redirect target as a process substitution only when its `(` is bare. A quoted or escaped `(` is file text.
2. Split a redirect glued to the lead word (`cd>f`, `cd>>f`) before reading the cd, so the cd and its redirect both apply.
3. Pin both shapes in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` with their bash 3.2 and 5 verdicts, per `.claude/skills/shell-scanner-bash-differential`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `echo x > '(x'` resolves `/r/(x`, and `cat <(true)` still resolves no target.
- `cd>f /main; cp a g.js` resolves `/r/f` and `/main/g.js`, so it is denied from a worktree whose main checkout is `/main`.
- Each rule has a red-turning mutant.
- The four scanner suites pass.

## Release Note

The worktree-always guard now catches a write to a quoted name starting with `(` and a `cd` written with a glued redirect.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — modify
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — modify

Origin: /claude-tweaks:build of #4303 (run 2026-10-25T143627-spec-4303), SDD Task 2 parked finding and final-review ruling

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

In `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`, a NAME=value assignment prefix, an `env` prefix or a `sudo` prefix hides every write shape. Each of these resolves `[]`, while bash 3.2 and 5 write or commit in the main checkout:

- `X=1 cp a /main/f.js`
- `sudo cp a /main/f.js`
- `X=1 tee /main/f.js`
- `X=1 sed -i s/a/b/ /main/f.js`
- `cd M; x+=1 git commit -m x` and `x+=1 git -C M commit -m x`

#4244's re-probe at HEAD (session cwd `/r`) adds `! cp x /M/b`, `time cp x /M/b` and `command cp x /M/b`: each gives `fileWriteTargets` `[]`.

A quoted name goes the other way. `"x"=1 cd /main` is read as an assignment plus a cd, but bash 3.2 and 5 run `x=1` as a command ("command not found") and stay put. That is a fail-open: from the main checkout, `"x"=1 cd /wt; cp a f.js` resolves only `/wt/f.js`, while bash writes the main checkout's `f.js`.

**Scope under ADR 0028 (#4571, 2026-10-30).** This record is a Phase 1 prerequisite of #4572. It owns every *stripped prefix* the recognised-shape set names:

- `NAME=value` / `NAME+=value`;
- `env` without `-S`/`--split-string`/`-P`;
- `sudo`/`doas` with their flags;
- `command` (except the `-v`/`-V` lookups);
- `builtin`, `exec`, `nice`, `nohup`, `time` and `!`.

#4244 then adds the compound keywords to the same helper. `pushd`/`popd` are unresolved cwds, which #4572 owns, not prefixes.

While in visitSegment, also replace the `while ((next = …) > cdLead)` assignment-in-condition loop (`git-command.js:~736`) with a plain loop.

## Deliverables

1. One "skip to command word" helper, used by `visitSegment`, `findGitLead` and the write-shape lead check. It skips leading NAME=value and NAME+=value words and the prefixes listed above, with their option flags, before reading the write-shape, git and cd lead.
2. Export the prefix set from `git-command.js`, so #4572's recogniser and #4244's keyword skip reuse it rather than retyping it.
3. Read a quoted-name assignment as bash does.
4. Pin each shape with its bash 3.2 and 5 verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every shape above resolves the path bash writes, so the write gate denies it from a worktree of a worktree-always repo. That includes `! cp x /M/b`, `time cp x /M/b`, `command cp x /M/b`, `nohup cp x /M/b`, `nice cp x /M/b`, `doas cp x /M/b` and `exec cp x /M/b`.
- `command -v cp` and `command -V cp` resolve no target, and bare `builtin` invents none.
- `"x"=1 cd /main` resolves no cd, so `"x"=1 cd /wt; cp a f.js` from the main checkout resolves the main checkout's `f.js`.
- A pin test fails if the exported prefix set and this record's list diverge.
- The base comparison is clean apart from the listed shapes.
- Each rule has a red-turning mutant.
- The four scanner suites pass.

## Release Note

The worktree-always guard now blocks a write into the main checkout behind a NAME=value, env, sudo or similar command prefix.

## Technical Approach

Follow the repo-local `shell-scanner-bash-differential` skill: judge each case against real bash 3.2 and 5, check base for regressions, and prove each rule with a mutant.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — modify (`visitSegment`, `findGitLead`, write-shape lead check, new exported prefix set)
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — modify
- `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js` — modify

## Gotchas

- `COMMAND_PREFIX_WORDS` (`git-command.js:~1420`) is used by `groupEvents` too. Adding `builtin`/`command` to it changes `groupEvents`, so decide in the PR whether they join that set or are skipped only at the lead checks.
- Draft PR #4530 was opened against this record's earlier scope and is on hold. Re-scope it to this body or close it.

**Related:** #4303, #4247

Origin: /claude-tweaks:build of #4303 (run 2026-10-25T143627-spec-4303), SDD Task 5 minor and final-review rounds

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s redirect scan reads a `>` comparison inside `$(( … ))` as a redirect. Bash 3.2 and 5 evaluate the comparison and write nothing, but the scanner reports a target:

- `echo $(( a>1 ))` resolves `/r/1`.
- `x=$(( 3>2 ))` resolves `2`.
- `(( a>1 || "${x:-")"}" ))` resolves `/r/1`, while bash gives a syntax error and writes nothing. Here `parenMatches` pairs quotes flatly, while `segmentSpansWith` nests `"` and `${`.

From the main checkout of a worktree-always repo, each of these is a spurious deny. All of them fail closed.

## Deliverables

1. Treat `>`, `>=`, `>>` and `<` inside `$(( ))`, `(( ))` and `$[ ]` as arithmetic operators, never as redirects.
2. Pin both shapes, plus a spaced form, with bash 3.2 and 5 verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Both shapes resolve no target.
- A real redirect after the arithmetic, as in `echo $(( 1>0 )) > /main/f.js`, still resolves `/main/f.js`.
- Each rule has a red-turning mutant.
- The four scanner suites pass.

## Release Note

The worktree-always guard no longer blocks a command whose only `>` is an arithmetic comparison.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — modify
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — modify

**Related:** #4303, #4242, #4247

Origin: /claude-tweaks:build of #4303 (run 2026-10-25T143627-spec-4303), SDD Task 5 ruling and final-review rounds

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s write gate does not walk the commands inside a `$( … )` or backtick body as their own segments. A write, mkdir or git command there resolves nothing, or resolves under the wrong cwd. Each shape below was checked against bash 3.2 and 5 from a worktree of a worktree-always repo:

- `echo $(cp a /main/f.js)` and ``echo `cp a /main/f.js` `` resolve no target. Bash writes `/main/f.js`.
- **N2:** a backtick holding a separator, followed by `&`, hides the rest of the command.
- **N3:** `((…))` as the first command in a substitution gives a spurious target.
- `echo $(( $(cd /main; cp a f.js) + 1 ))` resolves `/r/f.js`. Bash writes `/main/f.js`: the cd inside a substitution inside arithmetic is not followed.
- After a cwd-cap loss, a write inside `"$( cd …; … )"` (rr7's BVsub2/BVsub3) is allowed at every version, base included.

## Deliverables

1. Walk each substitution and backtick body as a nested command list. The body inherits the enclosing segment's cwd and gets its own cd scope, which it never leaks out, matching bash's subshell semantics.
2. Report the body's write, mkdir and git targets exactly as the top level does.
3. Pin every shape above in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js`, with its bash 3.2 and 5 verdict in the comment, per `.claude/skills/shell-scanner-bash-differential`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each shape above, run from a worktree of a worktree-always repo, is denied wherever bash 3.2 and 5 write into the main checkout.
- A base comparison of the #4149 routine table and the #4210 cases shows no allowed-to-denied move other than the listed ones.
- Every new rule has a mutant that turns a test red.
- The four scanner suites and `perf/heredoc-scan-linearity.test.js` pass.

## Release Note

The worktree-always guard now blocks a write into the main checkout made by a command inside $( ) or backticks.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — modify
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — modify

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3875, #3878, #3931, #4275, #4321, #4395

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:release --as X.Y.Z` is documented as the override for "a version the commits alone would not derive" (`plugin/skills/release/SKILL.md:18`, `:29`). Under `local-merge` it is passed to the engine as `release-local.js --release-as`. Two earlier stops make it unreachable in exactly the case it exists for, when the derived bump is `none`:

- **Preflight.** `bin/release-preflight.js` takes no `--as`. Its `proposedVersion` probe (`plugin/bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js:331`) throws `nothing to release: …` whenever `bumpPart(commits) === 'none'`. `SKILL.md:102`/`:116` route that error to Step 2's "print one line and stop" path, before the override is ever looked at. This is engine-agnostic: a pr-first range with no feat/fix also stops here.
- **Engine.** `plugin/bin/release-local.js:170-172` returns exit 3 on `part === 'none'` before `precheck(..., { releaseAs: opts.releaseAs })` runs at :174, so calling the engine directly with `--release-as` fails too.

Observed on 6.156.1, `local-merge`, tag `v1.2.3`. A GitHub merge-commit PR carrying two `feat(...)` commits plus one `docs(...)` commit reported `nothing to release since v1.2.3 (3 commit(s), none feat/fix/breaking; 2 unconventional)`. That is expected: #2954 keeps the first-parent walk for local-merge, so the `feat` commits sit behind the merge commit. `--as 1.3.0` then could not override it. The workaround was pushing an empty `feat(...)` marker commit to the default branch.

Secondary: the Step 2 line does not say that conventional commits exist off the first-parent line, which is the actual cause here.

## Deliverables

1. Let an explicit `--as` bypass the "nothing to release" stop at both layers. Pass `--as` to `release-preflight.js`, so that `proposedVersion` returns the override as `version` (with `part` derived from the override against `base`) instead of throwing. Make `release-local.js` skip its `part === 'none'` exit when `opts.releaseAs` is set, so `precheck`'s existing not-ahead validation (`usageError` → `UsageError` at :180) becomes the only gate.
2. Update `SKILL.md`'s Step 2 routing and the `--as` row so the override path is stated: with `--as`, a none-bump history continues to Step 4 with the override as the gating version.
3. Under local-merge, when the first-parent walk finds no feat/fix but the full history (`firstParent: false`) between the same refs does, add one line to the Step 2 message: `{N} conventional commit(s) off the first-parent line behind merge commits — pass --as <version> to release them`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `release-local.js --release-as 1.3.0` on a history whose bump is `none` proceeds to the precheck and releases v1.3.0. It does not exit 3.
- `release-local.js --release-as 1.2.3` (not ahead of v1.2.3) still fails with the existing "is not ahead of the current version" usage error.
- `release-preflight.js --as 1.3.0` on a none-bump history reports `proposedVersion.value.version === "1.3.0"` with no error. Without `--as`, the same history still yields the `nothing to release` error.
- In the merge-commit repro, the Step 2 line carries the off-first-parent hint. A history with no conventional commits anywhere prints the plain line unchanged.
- Tests cover each case in `tests/bin-lib/release-local/cli.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/release-preflight/pack.test.js` (plus `cli.test.js` there for the new flag).

## Release Note

`/claude-tweaks:release --as <version>` now works when the commits alone would not produce a release, and the "nothing to release" message points out conventional commits hidden behind merge commits.

## Technical Approach

The override is a user's explicit statement of the version, so it outranks the derived bump. The only safety check that still applies is "ahead of the current version", and `precheck` already enforces that. Keep the first-parent walk unchanged (#2954's ruling for local-merge); the hint in deliverable 3 only reports the off-line commits and does not count them toward the bump.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/release-local.js` — skip the `none` exit when `--release-as` is given
- `plugin/bin/release-preflight.js` — accept `--as`
- `plugin/bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js` — `proposedVersion` honours the override; off-first-parent hint data
- `plugin/skills/release/SKILL.md` — Step 2 routing and the `--as` row
- `tests/bin-lib/release-local/cli.test.js` — none-bump with and without `--release-as`
- `tests/bin-lib/release-preflight/pack.test.js` — `proposedVersion` with the override; off-first-parent hint
- `tests/bin-lib/release-preflight/cli.test.js` — `--as` flag parsing

## Gotchas

- Major-bump HARD-GATE: `SKILL.md:222` measures the gating version, which is `--as` when given. An override that jumps a major must still hit that gate, so derive `part` from the override against `base` instead of hard-coding `none`.
- Under pr-first the override reaches release-please as a `Release-As:` footer (`execute.md`). Check that preflight accepting `--as` does not change what pr-first pushes.

## Original request

release: --as / --release-as cannot override a "nothing to release" stop under local-merge

**Summary:** Under `integration-model: local-merge`, `/claude-tweaks:release --as X.Y.Z` cannot force a release when the derived bump is `none`. Both the preflight pack and `bin/release-local.js` stop at "nothing to release" before `--release-as` is checked.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** /claude-tweaks:release: `bin/release-local.js`, `bin/release-preflight.js` (`bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js`)

**Repro steps:**
1. Use a repo with `integration-model: local-merge` and tag `v1.2.3`.
2. On GitHub, merge a PR that holds two `feat(<scope>): …` commits, using the default merge-commit strategy. This puts a `Merge pull request #<N> from <org>/<branch>` commit on the first-parent line. Also add one `docs(<scope>): …` commit.
3. Run `/claude-tweaks:release`. Step 2 reports: `nothing to release since v1.2.3 (3 commit(s), none feat/fix/breaking; 2 unconventional)`. This is expected, because #2954's fix keeps the first-parent walk for local-merge.
4. Run `/claude-tweaks:release --as 1.3.0` to override.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: `--as 1.3.0` produces a v1.3.0 release. The SKILL.md Input table describes `--as` as the override for "a version the commits alone would not derive". It also says that under local-merge, `--as` is passed through as `release-local.js --release-as`.

Actual: `release-preflight.js` takes no `--as`, so `proposedVersion` falls back to `nothing to release` and Step 2 stops the run before Step 5. Calling the engine directly fails too: `bin/release-local.js` (around lines 169-172) exits with code 3 on `part === 'none'` before `precheck(..., { releaseAs })` runs. So `--release-as` can't be reached in exactly the case it exists for. The workaround was to push an empty `feat(<scope>): …` marker commit to the default branch.

Secondary: the Step 2 line says "none feat/fix/breaking" and gives no hint that conventional `feat:` commits sit behind the unconventional merge commits. A one-line note such as "N conventional commit(s) off the first-parent line behind merge commits" would have pointed straight at the cause.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.156.1

groups.body:
Origin: reflect full from #4421

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

Build, review and wrap-up all append rows to, and settle rows in, the run's open-items ledger (`docs/plans/*-ledger.md`, format in `plugin/skills/_shared/ledger-format.md`). The only sanctioned writer is `plugin/bin/stage-item.js --ledger` (`plugin/bin/lib/stage-item/ledger.js`), which appends a row paired with a staged file, under `{run-dir}/.ledger.lock`, through `atomic-write.js`. A plain row (a deferred minor, a fixed review finding) and a status/resolution settle have no CLI, so a worktree session writes them by hand.

The obvious hand-written forms — `node -e` with quoted table cells or `>=`, a heredoc, `printf … >>` — are refused by the harness's worktree-isolation compound-Bash guard. Run `2026-10-26T123848-spec-4336-4419-4420-4421` (records #4336, #4419, #4420, #4421) logged 42 such refusals (`wd-guard-refusal`, `harness-worktree-isolation`), many of them ledger writes, and finished its ledger edits through ad-hoc scratchpad scripts that bypass the lock and atomic write.

## Deliverables

- [ ] A `plugin/bin/hooks.js ledger-row` verb (or a sibling CLI) that appends one row (`--phase`, `--item`, `--status`, optional `--resolution`) or settles an existing row by number (`--row N --status … --resolution …`), reusing `stage-item/ledger.js`'s lock, re-read and atomic write and `wrap-up/ledger-write.js`'s table parser/serializer, with `escapeLedgerCell` for pipes
- [ ] Validate `--status` against `ledger-format.md`'s closed enum (`open`, `fixed`, `deferred`, `accepted`, `acknowledged`, `observation`) and its resolution-text requirements (`fixed` needs a commit or file ref; `deferred` needs origin, files and trigger)
- [ ] Point the build/review/wrap-up prose that appends or settles ledger rows at the verb

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From a linked worktree, `node plugin/bin/hooks.js ledger-row --ledger <path> --phase build --item "a | b" --status open` appends one row whose Item cell keeps the escaped pipe, under the ledger lock.
2. `--row 3 --status fixed --resolution "abc123"` rewrites only row 3's Status and Resolution cells; `--status resolved` exits non-zero naming the enum.
3. A concurrent append from two processes yields two distinct row numbers (test with two child processes).
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Pipeline phases record and settle open-items ledger rows through one safe command instead of hand-edited table lines.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — new ledger-row verb
- `plugin/bin/lib/stage-item/ledger.js` — share the lock/re-read/atomic-write path
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ledger-format.md` — name the writer

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (deferred validation): No literal `origin:`/`files:`/`trigger:` labels. `ledger-row` accepts `--status deferred` only when its Resolution (a) names a `staged/…` path or a record reference, or (b) carries exactly one valid `Defer-reason:` from `_shared/deferral-gate.md`. The checks for (a) and (b) reuse `pack.js`'s predicates (`LEDGER_DEFERRED_STAGED_RE`/`namesRecordReference` for `deferredUnstaged`, `hasValidDeferReason`), exported rather than copied. A row accepted only under (b) is written, and the JSON output flags it `incompleteDeferral: true`; the resolve gate settles it later. A `deferred` Resolution meeting neither (a) nor (b) exits non-zero, names the rule, and writes nothing.
- Q2 (terminal rows): Reading A — `ledger-row --row N` reads row N's current Status first. If it is terminal (`fixed`, `deferred`, `accepted`, `acknowledged`, `observation`), the verb exits 1 with nothing written and names the row and its status. The one exception is an incomplete deferral: a `deferred` row whose Resolution names neither a `staged/…` path nor a record reference, per `pack.js`'s `deferredUnstaged` predicate. That row may be settled to any terminal status, since that is its first complete terminal write per `_shared/ledger-format.md`.

Origin: Review Console, human-approved — #4285 low-confidence review findings and hindsight (run 2026-10-26T131247-spec-4290-4285-4396, PR #4427)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

#4285 added `tests/helpers/path-stub.js` (`STUB_SKIP`, `installStub`, `pathWithOnly`). It chose which tests skip on win32 from one Windows run's failing list. The rule the windows-checkout-test-parity skill now states is different: judge each test by whether it writes a stub and whether its assertion depends on that stub running. A failing list never shows a test that passes vacuously, so the two selections differ.

A scripted audit of the six installStub suites found 22 stub-installing tests with no `STUB_SKIP`. They are in `tests/reconcile.test.js` at 1463-1581 (reconcileWithAsyncMerge), 2961/2970/2995 (reconcileWithRecordedResolver) and 3125-3258 (the #4180 dryRunFixture group), plus `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/prune-remote.test.js:407` and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` at 168/250/572/746/810. The stub never runs on windows-latest, so several of these pass vacuously. Their assertions are things only the stub can make true or false: `ghCalls() === ''`, `fetchCalls` deep-equal to `[]`, and the batch-fail fallback path. A review agent no-op'd the stub on reconcile 3125 and 1469 and on prune-remote 407, and each still printed `ok 1`. reap-merged 746/810 skip on a chmod reason (`MID_DELETE_SKIP`), not on `STUB_SKIP`.

Single-stub `gh` wrappers outside the helper still hand-roll the install, so their temp dirs leak and their win32 skip reasons differ: `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` (105/141), `tests/console-execute.test.js:469`, `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js:523` and `tests/hooks-resolve-console.test.js:82`. In reap-merged.test.js:287 the stub is installed before a worktree-lock call that can throw, outside the try that restores it.

The helper's own pin suite has two gaps. `tests/path-stub-helper.test.js:86` is titled as a PATHEXT test, but the binary lookup never consults PATHEXT, and no case excludes a `gh.CMD`. The `STUB_SKIP` pin at :28 reduces to `=== false` off win32.

## Deliverables

- Go through the 22 tests one at a time. Add `{ skip: STUB_SKIP }` where the assertion depends on the stub running. Where a test keeps running on win32, add a comment saying its assertions hold whatever answers on PATH. reap-merged 746/810 skip with the stub reason when the stub is what fails there.
- Move the single-stub hand-rolled wrappers listed above onto `installStub` with `STUB_SKIP`. The multi-stub wrappers the parity skill names stay hand-rolled.
- Move reap-merged.test.js:287's stub install inside the try that restores it.
- In `tests/path-stub-helper.test.js`, retitle the :86 test to what the lookup actually does, add an excluded-`gh.CMD` case, and give the :28 pin a win32 assertion by injecting the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1.1: re-running the stub-dependence audit over the installStub suites reports no stub-installing test that lacks both `STUB_SKIP` and a comment explaining why it holds on win32.
- AC1.2: a `windows-regression.yml` run on the branch lists no newly failing file, and each test that newly skips reports `# SKIP win32: execFile resolves only .exe/.com on PATH, so a script stub is never spawned` in `verify-logs/tests.log`.
- AC2.1: none of the listed single-stub wrappers writes its own temp dir or PATH entry any more (a grep for `mkdtemp` beside `PATH =` in those files comes back empty).
- AC3.1: `tests/path-stub-helper.test.js` has a case where an excluded `gh.CMD` on PATH makes `pathWithOnly` exclude that directory, and a win32 `STUB_SKIP` assertion.

## Release Note

Internal: tests that fake `git`/`gh` now skip on Windows whenever their result depends on the fake running, instead of passing without testing anything.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `tests/reconcile.test.js` — STUB_SKIP on the stub-dependent tests
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/prune-remote.test.js` — STUB_SKIP on the batch-fail fallback test
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` — STUB_SKIP on stub-dependent tests; stub install inside the try
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — single-stub gh helpers onto installStub
- `tests/console-execute.test.js` — gh stub onto installStub
- `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` — gh stub onto installStub
- `tests/hooks-resolve-console.test.js` — gh stub onto installStub
- `tests/path-stub-helper.test.js` — retitle the PATHEXT test, add a gh.CMD exclude case and a win32 STUB_SKIP pin

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s queue pull runs a shipped-candidate exclusion (#1984, `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md:505-560`). `classifyShipped` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js:47`) rates a merged PR that mentions the record, merged after the record was created, as `weak`; with title-similarity or `### Key Files` coverage it becomes `strong`, and a `strong` record is dropped from `dispatch-groups.json` with a staged `staged/shipped-close-N.md` proposing `gh issue close N`. The #4314 fix skips mentions whose PR was opened before the record existed.

Observed on 6.155.0 (rule unchanged in 6.156.1): two records built API-first — PR A shipped the API half with `Refs #N` (a deliberate non-closing reference), the pipeline released the claim with a reason naming the remaining UI half, and the record stayed open with `auto:build`. The next `/claude-tweaks:dispatch #N` logged `#N excluded, shipped by merged PR #A (merged-pr-mention-after-created, title-similarity)` (the second record: `key-files-covered`), removed both records with no bypass, and staged close proposals. Approving them would close unfinished records; the only workaround was `/claude-tweaks:flow #N` directly.

What the detector sees: `fetchLinkedPRs` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/linked-prs.js:69-72`) gives each mention only `{number, title, state, merged, mergedAt, createdAt}` — nothing about whether the reference closes the record, and nothing about the record's own claim history. A non-closing reference alone cannot be the signal: the instances the detector was built for (#1791/#1803, #1484/#1857) were merged PRs that shipped everything without a closing keyword. The distinguishing fact here is that a pipeline **released the record's claim after PR A merged** — `release-claim.js` writes an `agent-claim-release` marker comment and a `released: true` tombstone, both carrying `releasedAt` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/claims.js:56-66`). A release after the merge means a run saw the merge and deliberately left the record open.

## Deliverables

1. Give `classifyShipped` the record's latest claim-release time (from the claims-registry tombstone `dispatch` already reads, or the latest `agent-claim-release` comment marker). A mention whose `mergedAt` is earlier than that release never rates `strong`; it rates `weak` at most, so the record stays dispatchable.
2. Feed that value from the queue pull's two `classifyShipped` call sites in `queue-pull-script.md`, via whichever read is cheapest at that point (a claim-reader read for the candidate records, or a `comments` field added to `buildLinkedPRQuery`'s batched GraphQL).
3. Log the downgrade so the exclusion decision stays auditable, e.g. `#N kept: merged PR #A predates claim release at {releasedAt} — remaining work declared`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record mentioned by a merged PR with title-similarity, whose claim was released after that PR's `mergedAt`, classifies `weak` (not excluded, no `shipped-close-N.md` staged).
- The same record with no release after the merge still classifies `strong`, so the #1791/#1803-style detection is unchanged.
- A release *before* the PR merged does not downgrade (it predates the PR's evidence).
- A missing or unreadable release time never downgrades and never upgrades (the prior behavior holds).
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js` covers all four cases; `tests/dispatch-shipped-candidate-prose.test.js` still passes with the updated call sites.

## Release Note

Dispatch no longer treats a record as already shipped when a pipeline merged only part of it and released the record to finish the rest.

## Technical Approach

The reporter offered two signals: a non-closing reference (`Refs #N`) where a closing keyword was available, and a claim-release reason naming remaining work. The release *time* is chosen over both. The keyword alone cannot distinguish this case from the historical no-keyword ships the detector exists for. Parsing the reason text for "remaining work" is free-text judgment, while "released after the merge" is a timestamp comparison on data the plugin itself writes. Keep `classifyShipped` pure: the caller passes `opts.lastReleasedAt` (ISO or null) the same way it already passes `opts.prFiles`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js` — release-time downgrade rule
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/linked-prs.js` — only if the release time is read via the batched GraphQL
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/claims.js` — reference: release marker and tombstone shape
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — pass the release time at both `classifyShipped` call sites; log the downgrade
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js` — four-case coverage
- `tests/dispatch-shipped-candidate-prose.test.js` — prose pins for the call sites

## Gotchas

- Sweeps also release claims (`release-claim.js --reason ... ` from `/claude-tweaks:specify`'s drain and `/claude-tweaks:tidy`'s stale-claim backstop). A shaping-only release after a merge would also downgrade. That is the safe direction (the record stays dispatchable, and the build's own shipped-exit check, `tests/build-already-shipped-exit.test.js`, still catches a truly shipped record), but say so in the code comment.
- Compare instants, not strings: `mergedAt` and `releasedAt` are both ISO, but normalize through `Date` as the existing createdAt checks do.

## Original request

dispatch: shipped-candidate exclusion treats an API-first half PR's non-closing "Refs #N" as shipping the whole record

**Summary:** `bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js`'s `classifyShipped` rated two open records `strong` (already shipped) because a merged PR mentioned each with a non-closing reference (`Refs #N` / `(refs #N)`) plus title-similarity or key-files-covered — but both PRs were the deliberate API-first half of a two-PR record whose UI half was still unbuilt.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** dispatch queue pull — shipped-candidate exclusion (#1984), `bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js`, `skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md`

**Repro steps:**
1. A record whose Deliverables span an API route and a UI section is built API-first (the project ships the API half in one PR and the UI half in a later one): PR A implements the API half, its body states it references the record without closing it, its fixes block carries `Refs #N` (no closing keyword), and its title matches the record's title (or its changed files cover the record's `### Key Files`). PR A merges.
2. The pipeline releases the record's claim with a reason naming the remaining work, e.g. agent-claim-release `{"reason":"merged API half: PR A; UI half still to build"}`, and the record stays open with `auto:build` for the UI half.
3. Run `/claude-tweaks:dispatch #N` (or an explicit list containing it).

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: a merged PR that only references the record with a non-closing keyword, on a record whose own claim-release reason says work remains, is at most `weak` — the record stays dispatchable.
Actual: queue pull logs `#N excluded, shipped by merged PR #A (merged-pr-mention-after-created, title-similarity)` (second instance: `key-files-covered`), removes the record from `dispatch-groups.json` with no `#N` bypass, and stages `staged/shipped-close-N.md` proposing `gh issue close N --comment "Deliverables already shipped by #A"`. Approving that proposal would close an unfinished record. Two records hit this in one firing. The only workaround is to bypass dispatch and run `/claude-tweaks:flow #N` directly.

The #4314 fix (skip a mention whose PR was opened before the record was created) does not cover this: here the record predates the PR. Possible signals the detector could use: the mention is a non-closing reference while a closing keyword was available (`Refs`/`refs` vs `Fixes`/`Closes`), and/or the record's latest agent-claim-release reason names remaining work.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.156.1 (observed on 6.155.0; `classifyShipped`'s strong-tier rule is unchanged in 6.156.1)

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3813, #4347, #4395

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:design-wrapper review` mode's Step 5 (`plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md:428`) writes its audit findings cache to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{feature}-audit.json` (fallback `docs/plans/audit-{spec-slug}.json`). The file is untracked, not gitignored, and not a declared `generated` path, so writing it makes the tree dirty: `verify.js --stamp-status` reports `"dirty":true,"verifiedHead":false`, and every later consumer of the pass stamp (`plugin/skills/test/verification.md:187` — `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5's Skip-if-recent, polish's re-verify, wrap-up) treats that as "no recent pass". The same review call that just relied on the stamp invalidates it.

Observed on 6.155.0 (path unchanged in 6.156.1): a `/claude-tweaks:flow #N review,polish,wrap-up auto` run on a UI record. After design-wrapper review wrote the cache, `git status --short` showed `?? docs/plans/{date}-{feature}-audit.json` and the stamp went dirty. The agent deleted the cache to recover (its findings were all info-level); a run whose findings carry suggestions would have had to commit the cache or pay a full re-verify.

The cache is per-run, advisory, and never committed: `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md:50` reads it (an absent cache is a no-op — `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/command-map.md:86`), and wrap-up deletes it after the spec ships (`plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md:17`, `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js:318`). `verification.md` defines `generated` as paths the declared checks themselves regenerate, which does not describe this cache.

Survey mode writes two siblings with the same exposure: `-recommendations.json` (`plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/survey.md:68`) and `-declined.json` (`survey.md:42`, written by `/flow`'s decline detection). `-declined.json` is cross-run state (decline tracking per spec); the other two are per-run.

## Deliverables

1. Move the review-mode audit cache to the pipeline run directory (`$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, resolved per `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`), keeping the `docs/plans/` fallback path only for a review invoked with no run directory — update the writer (`modes/review.md` Step 5) and every reader (`modes/polish.md`, `command-map.md`).
2. Update wrap-up's design-wrapper cache cleanup (`cleanup-procedures.md` row 3, `cleanup-procedures-execution.md`, `engine-verify.js`'s suffix list) so it still finds and removes the cache at its new location (or drops the per-run cache from cleanup if run-dir archival already covers it), without breaking cleanup of legacy `docs/plans/*-audit.json` files.
3. Apply the same relocation to the per-run `-recommendations.json` cache. For the cross-run `-declined.json` cache, either move it to a gitignored `.claude-tweaks/` path that survives across runs, or record in this record why it stays where it is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After design-wrapper review mode writes its audit cache inside a pipeline run with a verified-HEAD stamp, `git status --short` lists no new untracked file and `verify.js --stamp-status` still reports `verifiedHead: true`.
- Polish mode reads the relocated audit cache and dispatches the same suggestion-driven commands it did from the old path (test with a fixture cache at the new location).
- Wrap-up cleanup removes the relocated cache, and still removes a legacy `docs/plans/*-audit.json` when one is present.
- `-declined.json` decline tracking still suppresses a twice-declined recommendation in a later run.

## Release Note

The design review's findings cache no longer dirties the working tree, so later pipeline steps keep trusting the earlier test pass instead of re-running it.

## Technical Approach

The record offers two fixes: relocate the cache, or have the stamp's dirty check exempt `docs/plans/*-audit.json`. Relocation is chosen: the cache is per-run advisory state with no reason to live in a tracked directory, and an exemption would teach the stamp about one skill's file names. The run directory is already where per-run artifacts live and is gitignored except for `work/` specs. Keep path resolution in one place (a small resolver both writer and readers call, or a single documented rule in `modes/review.md` that `polish.md` and `command-map.md` cite) so the three files cannot drift.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` — Step 5 cache path
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` — cache read path resolution
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/command-map.md` — suggestion-driven step's cache reference
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/survey.md` — recommendations/declined cache paths
- `plugin/skills/flow/survey.md` — decline detection, the `-declined.json` writer
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures.md` — design wrapper cache cleanup row
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — cleanup path resolution
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` — cache suffix list at :318

## Gotchas

- Resolve the run directory under `$RUN_ROOT` (the main checkout), never relative to the worktree cwd — a relative path from a worktree silently shadows the main run dir (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`).
- Multi-spec runs namespace per-spec artifacts (`plugin/skills/flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`); the audit cache must land in the spec's own run subdirectory so two specs' caches never collide.
- `survey.md:68`'s note that the cache "keeps survey state out of `~/.claude-tweaks/`" refers to the user-home directory, not the project's `.claude-tweaks/`; a project-local gitignored path does not contradict it.

## Original request

design-wrapper: review mode's audit cache in docs/plans/ dirties the verification pass stamp

**Summary:** `/claude-tweaks:design-wrapper review` writes its audit findings cache to `docs/plans/{date}-{feature}-audit.json`, an untracked, non-ignored, non-`generated` path, so the write flips `verify.js --stamp-status` to `dirty: true, verifiedHead: false` inside the same review call that just relied on the stamp.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** design-wrapper (review mode audit cache, `command-map.md` / `modes/polish.md`) and the verification pass stamp (`verify.js --stamp-status`)

**Repro steps:**
1. Run `/claude-tweaks:flow #N review,polish,wrap-up auto` on a UI record in a project whose verify-scope declaration has no `generated` glob covering `docs/plans/`, with the first call's runner stamp verifying HEAD.
2. Let review reach design-wrapper review mode, which writes `docs/plans/{date}-{feature}-audit.json`.
3. Run `git status --short` → `?? docs/plans/{date}-{feature}-audit.json`; run `verify.js --stamp-status` → `"dirty":true,"verifiedHead":false`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: a review that writes its own advisory cache does not invalidate the pass stamp the same review just read (review Step 1.5), so polish and wrap-up can keep trusting it.
Actual: every later gate (polish re-verify, wrap-up) must either commit the cache, delete it, or re-run the full verification. In the observed run the agent deleted the cache (all findings were info-level with no suggestion); a run whose findings carry suggestions would have had to commit it or pay a full re-verify. `verification.md` defines `generated` as paths the declared checks themselves regenerate, which does not describe this cache.

Suggested fix: write the cache under the run directory (or another `.claude-tweaks/` path projects already ignore) — polish already tolerates an absent cache — or have the stamp's dirty check exempt `docs/plans/*-audit.json` the way it exempts declared `generated` paths.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.156.1 (observed on 6.155.0; the cache path in `skills/design-wrapper/command-map.md` and `modes/polish.md` is unchanged in 6.156.1)
