**Related:** #4245

Origin: /claude-tweaks:release v6.154.1 whole-branch review, delta 43c11df0e..5fb12cb2c (run 2026-10-21T194624-release-standalone, staged/review-36.md); reproduced by an executed probe in /bin/bash 3.2 and Homebrew bash 5

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` (~line 1442, the heredoc keep/strip decision) keeps an unquoted heredoc body visible to the write scan only when the body matches `/\$\(|`/`. Bash removes backslash-newline from an unquoted heredoc body before expansion, so `$\` at the end of one line followed by `(echo hi > w)` on the next is a command substitution that runs and writes `w`. The literal text holds no `$(`, so the scanner strips the body as data and `fileWriteTargets` returns `[]`.

Probe: `cat <<EOF\n$\\\n(echo hi > w_cont)\nEOF\n`. Scanner targets: `[]`. File `w_cont` is written by both `/bin/bash` 3.2 and bash 5. A write into the main checkout passes the worktree-always gate this way.

Pre-existing. Before #4149 the scanner missed even a plain `$(…)` heredoc write; #4149 closed the plain case, not this one. #4245 (backslash-newline outside heredoc bodies) explicitly leaves heredoc body lines unchanged, so it does not cover this.

## Deliverables

1. Before testing an unquoted heredoc body for expansions, join backslash-newline pairs the way bash does for unquoted bodies (a quoted delimiter `<<'EOF'` leaves the body literal and stays stripped).

2. Apply the same joined text to the backtick test, so `` `\<newline>cmd` `` forms are caught too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fileWriteTargets('cat <<EOF\n$\\\n(echo hi > w)\nEOF\n', cwd)` resolves `w`.

- `fileWriteTargets("cat <<'EOF'\n$\\\n(echo hi > w)\nEOF\n", cwd)` still returns `[]` (quoted delimiter: bash writes nothing).

- A test in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` pins both cases and goes red when the fix is reverted; the shell-scanner bash differential agrees with bash on both.

- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

The worktree-always write gate now catches a command substitution split across lines with a backslash inside an unquoted heredoc.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — join backslash-newline in unquoted heredoc bodies before the keep test
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — continuation-in-heredoc cases

groups.body:
**Related:** #4212, #4210, #4247

Origin: dispatch close-out of PR #4223 (record #4212), 2026-10-25

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

After #4210 (PR #4235, merge `b4a2f59db`), `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s `tokenize` returns a per-character `spanKinds` mask and keeps backslashes in token values as typed; `isUnresolvable` then rejects any token still carrying a backslash. Measured on main (2026-10-25) against #4212's test expectations, three classes resolve **no** target where bash writes to a concrete path. All three are fail-open: none fabricates a target.

1. **Escaped blank in a path word:** `mkdir a\ b`, `mkdir -p /r/a\ b/c`, `cp a my\ file.js`, `cd /r/a\ b && git commit -m x` return `[]`; bash targets `/r/a b`, `/r/a b/c`, `/r/my file.js`, `/r/a b`.
2. **Backslash-newline line continuation** inside or before a word: `echo x >/ma\<newline>in/x` and `mkdir -p \<newline>/abs/dir` return `[]`; bash targets `/main/x` and `/abs/dir`.
3. **A `$` / `${…}` / backtick word, then an escaped blank, then `>`:** `echo $M\ >x`, `echo ${M}\ >x`, ``echo `d`\ >x``, `echo $M\ bar>x` return `[]`; bash redirects to `x`. `echo $M>x` staying `[]` is the documented gap and must not change.

PR #4223 (record #4212, branch `worktree-dispatch-record-4212`, tip `9a6fc75a9`) implemented all three by unescaping values in the old regex tokenizer. It was closed unmerged: it predates the span mask, conflicts with it in all four touched files, and lacks #4210's quoted-span and `(ls)>out` resolution. #4212's own acceptance criteria already pass on main.

## Deliverables

- `tokenize` yields the unescaped value for an escaped blank in a bare word and for an escaped double quote, and deletes a backslash-newline pair before word splitting, while keeping `spanKinds[i].length === tokens[i].length` (the mask must shrink with the value) and keeping every other backslash pair verbatim (Windows paths, `\'`).
- The glued-redirect scan resolves the operand after an escaped blank that follows a `$`/backtick prefix (`$M\ >x`), without accepting `$M>x`.
- `isUnresolvable` stops rejecting a token whose only backslashes were unescaped by the tokenizer.
- `docs/journeys/write-a-glued-redirect-from-the-main-checkout-4015.md` and the redirect paragraph in `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` describe the new behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every case listed in Current State resolves the bash target named there, pinned in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` / `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js`, each going red when the change is reverted.
- #4212's carried-over expectations hold on the new code: `echo "a\" b>c "` → none, `echo foo>x` → `x`, `echo foo\\>x` → `x`, `echo foo\>x` → none, `cd \'/wt\' && git commit` → none, `echo x > \'/abs/f\'` → none, `echo $M>x` → none, and `echo a\"b>c` → `c` (bash's actual target; #4212 had pinned it as a known miss).
- #4210's cases still resolve (`echo "hi">x` → `x`, `(ls)>out` → `out`), and the existing `fileWriteTargets` / `gitTargets` / `mkdirTargets` suites pass unchanged.
- Full `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

The worktree-always gate now sees writes to a path with an escaped space, a path split by a line continuation, and a redirect after a `$VAR\ ` word, which it previously let through.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — modify
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — modify
- `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js` — modify
- `docs/journeys/write-a-glued-redirect-from-the-main-checkout-4015.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` — modify

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (AC2 escaped single quotes): Reading B — amend AC2 so `cd \'/wt\' && git commit` → `{cwd}/'/wt'` (`/r/'/wt'`) and `echo x > \'/abs/f\'` → `{cwd}/'/abs/f'` (`/r/'/abs/f'`). These are bash's relative targets, as #4281's test "an escaped quote in a word is a literal character" pins. Every other AC2 expectation stands unchanged, and no #4281 pin is reverted.
- Q2 (Deliverable 1 verbatim clause): Reading B — #4281 supersedes the clause "keeping every other backslash pair verbatim (Windows paths, `\'`)". Tokens are bash word values (`tokenize("cp a C:\\r\\x \\'/wt\\'")` → `C:rx`, `'/wt'`), the typed text stays in `typed`, and `spanKinds[i].length === tokens[i].length` still holds. No task restores verbatim pairs.
- Q3 (AC1 red-on-revert): Reading B — AC1's "each going red when the change is reverted" covers the class-3 pins only. The six class-1/2 cases, which #4281 already resolves on main, are pinned as characterization tests. Each is shown to go red against an uncommitted scratch mutant of #4281's `tokenize` unescaping lines, and that mutant result is quoted in the build report.
- Q4 ($NAME after the last escaped blank): Reading A — the text after the last escaped blank follows the plain-word rule, so `echo $M\ $N>x` and `echo ${M}\ ${N}>x` stay `[]`, the same as `echo $M>x`. Pin both as known misses citing #4328, whose deliverable "Read a glued redirect after a word whose bare `$` part is a plain parameter reference" owns them.

Origin: #4279 — windows-regression run 40197254500 after #4205 (main d5efeed1c), folded into the #2767 class split

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #4279, #4205, #4028, #2767, and the class H record from the #2767 split (it takes #4279's `hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js:1638` failure)

## Current State

On a Windows-native path, the PreToolUse `updatedInput` normalizer (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.js`, #4205) declines two of its rules. The cause is in this file's own literal-character classes, not in `git-command.js`'s backslash rule:

- **`plugin-root-placeholder`** (line 525). Line 528 returns `null` unless `LITERAL_VALUE.test(pluginRoot)`. `LITERAL_VALUE` (line 51, `/^[A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,=-][A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,= -]*$/`) excludes `\`. On win32 the root is native (`DEFAULT_PLUGIN_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, …)`, line 44; the test's `ROOT` sits under `os.tmpdir()`), so the rule never fires.
- **`drop-redundant-cd`** (line 653). `LEADING_CD` (line 642) admits a double-quoted target only from `[^"$`\\]*`, and an unquoted one only from a class with no `\`. `` cd "D:\…\cwd" && `` never matches, so the rule returns `null`.

Both declines are safe, since the command passes through unchanged. Their effect is that on Windows the normalizer never respells these shapes, so the harness worktree-isolation refusals they exist to avoid still happen there.

The evidence in #4279: each failing assertion expects a rewrite and gets `+ null`. All 3 are in 1 file (line numbers as of d5efeed1c).

### Failing tests

- `tests/bin-lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.test.js:119` — plugin-root-placeholder substitutes the injected root and skips when the command assigns it
- `tests/bin-lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.test.js:144` — plugin-root-placeholder inlines only a file under its own bin/
- `tests/bin-lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.test.js:281` — drop-redundant-cd drops cd "<cwd>" && only when it resolves to cwd

## Deliverables

- `rewriteForGuard` takes a `pathImpl` option, defaulting to `path`, and passes it to the rules for `isAbsolute`/`sep`. It reads `lstatType`/`canonicalRealpath` through `deps`, so a `path.win32` case runs on Linux.
- `plugin-root-placeholder` inlines the root as `toPosix(pluginRoot, pathImpl.sep)`. `D:/…` passes `LITERAL_VALUE` and means the same quoted or bare. `shippedUnder` still lstat's the native join.
- `drop-redundant-cd` accepts a double-quoted target whose backslashes all precede a character other than `$`, `` ` ``, `"`, `\` or newline, so bash keeps them literally. It still requires the exact spelling of the cwd. An unquoted backslash target still declines, because bash strips those backslashes.
- In `tests/bin-lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.test.js`, the expected commands at `:119` and `:144` are built from the forward-slashed root.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: `node --test tests/bin-lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.test.js tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` passes on Linux, including the bash+zsh equivalence and property cases the `pretooluse-updatedinput-normalizer` skill requires.
2. AC2: a Linux-runnable win32 pin through `pathImpl: path.win32` and injected deps. `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/x.js" a` with root `D:\\p\\root` rewrites to exactly `node "D:/p/root/bin/x.js" a`. `cd "D:\\w\\cwd" && ls x` with that cwd rewrites to `ls x`. The unquoted `cd D:\\w\\cwd && ls x` and the double-quoted `cd "D:\\w\\$X" && ls x` both decline.
3. AC3: go-red. With the `toPosix` or the `LEADING_CD` change reverted, AC2's positive cases return `null`.
4. AC4: a `windows-regression.yml` dispatch on the branch shows `tests/bin-lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.test.js` with 0 failures and no newly failing file.

## Release Note

Windows: the Bash-command normalizer now inlines `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and drops a redundant leading `cd "<cwd>" &&`, as it already does on macOS and Linux.

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the harness worktree-isolation guard treats a forward-slashed plugin root path (`D:/…`) like the native one. If it does not, inline the native root, but only into double-quoted references.
- Per the normalizer skill, a changed rule needs new positive equivalence cases and one must-decline case per new bail condition. The shell tests skip on win32, so AC2's `path.win32` pin is the Linux CI cover.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.js` — `pathImpl` and fs deps seams, forward-slashed root inlining, backslash-tolerant double-quoted `LEADING_CD`
- `tests/bin-lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.test.js` — `path.win32` pins, forward-slashed expectations, equivalence and decline cases

Origin: #2767 class split — classification of windows-regression run 40169646104 (main 6a41ebe3a)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #2767, #3702, #3064, #4222 (the same fix for `tests/bin-lib/verify/cli.test.js`), #3982 (owns `tests/reconcile.test.js:488`), #3695

## Current State

Git for Windows prints paths with forward slashes. `rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `worktree list --porcelain` print `D:/a/_temp/…`, and `ls-files` and `status` print repo-relative `a/b/c`. These tests build their expected value with the native `path.join`, which gives `D:\a\_temp\…` and `a\b\c`, so the comparison fails on win32 only. Under the #3064 calibration, git's own spelling is the correct value and the test is what needs fixing.

- `tests/bin-lib/verify/baseline.test.js:913`: `realGit.listWorktrees` output does not `includes(normalWt)`, a native path.
- `tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js:13`, `:114`, `:264`: `runGit`/`runGitAsync` return `D:/a/_temp/ct-wtd-…`, and the test expects the native temp dir.
- `tests/run-integrity.test.js:176`: `worktreePathForBranch` returns the porcelain path `D:/…/.claude/worktrees/feat`.
- `tests/teardown-gate.test.js:550`: the `wd-foreign-teardown` event's `path` carries `D:/…/wt`.
- `tests/tidy-residue-markers.test.js:305`, `:344`: git-listed `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/…/decisions.md` against a `path.join` expectation.

Excluded on purpose: `tests/bin-lib/verify/cli.test.js:3425` (#4222) and `tests/reconcile.test.js:488` (#3982).

8 tests in 5 files fail on Windows (line numbers as of 988cc584d).

### Failing tests

- `tests/bin-lib/verify/baseline.test.js:913` — realGit.listWorktrees reads real `git worktree list` output, and findStaleBaselineWorktrees names only the stale scratch one (#3064)
- `tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js:13` — runGit: success returns trimmed stdout and a null failure
- `tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js:114` — runGitAsync: success returns trimmed stdout and a null failure
- `tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js:264` — runGit: a non-numeric or non-positive CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS falls back to DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS
- `tests/run-integrity.test.js:176` — worktreePathForBranch: finds the live linked worktree checked out on the given branch
- `tests/teardown-gate.test.js:550` — AC5: a foreign-owned run warns instead of denying, and logs wd-foreign-teardown
- `tests/tidy-residue-markers.test.js:305` — #1493 C1: Step 7.5's copy+add lands decisions.md, report.md, and staged/** in the worktree's own commit
- `tests/tidy-residue-markers.test.js:344` — #1494 review fix: Step 7.5's copy+add also lands in a *-sweep-standalone* run dir's worktree commit

## Deliverables

- For an absolute path that git printed, derive the expected value from git's own output, as #4222 does. For example, `hooks-git-exec.test.js` compares against `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run by the test itself, and `baseline.test.js` and `run-integrity.test.js` take the porcelain entry whose path ends in the fixture directory. No `process.platform` branch.
- Build a repo-relative ID that git lists with `path.posix.join`, or with `toPosix` on the test's own `path.join`, in `tidy-residue-markers.test.js`.

groups.body:
Origin: #2767 class split — classification of windows-regression run 40169646104 (main 6a41ebe3a)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #2767, #4146 (this record takes its A part)

## Current State

These tests hard-code a POSIX absolute fixture path (`/repo`, `/x`, `/rd`, `/run/primary`, `/wt/explicit`, `/runs`, `/srv/content`) where the code under test runs that path through `path.resolve` or `path.join`. On win32, `path.resolve('/repo')` is `D:\repo` and `path.join('/x', 'y')` is `\x\y`. So either the expected literal no longer matches, or a fake fs or fake reader keyed on the literal is never hit. The `windows-checkout-test-parity` skill's `path.resolve` Anti-Patterns row names this class. The shapes by file:

- `tests/apply-refine-labels.test.js` (4): expects `'/repo/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/run-1'` and gets `'D:\\repo\\.claude-tweaks\\pipelines\\run-1'`.
- `tests/bin-lib/atomic-write.test.js` (2), `tests/bin-lib/json-store.test.js` (1): `startsWith('/x/store….tmp-')` against a tmp path the code builds with `path.join`.
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/impact.test.js:334`: expects `'\\repo\\.git'` (a join) where the code resolves to `'D:\\repo\\.git'`.
- `tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/server.test.js:102`: `resolveSafe` returns `'\\srv\\content\\'`, and the test expects `'/srv/content'`.
- `tests/friction-events-cli.test.js` (5): `'/wt/explicit'` and `'/run/primary'` literals, plus a fake `readEvents` keyed on `'/run/primary'` while the CLI passes the resolved key.
- `tests/hooks-context.test.js:855`: expects `'/runs/…'` where the code joins to `'\\runs\\…'`.
- `tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js` (5): a fake fs keyed `'/rd/…'` that `path.join` never reaches, so no reversals are read.

20 tests in 8 files fail on Windows (line numbers as of 988cc584d).

### Failing tests

- `tests/apply-refine-labels.test.js:229` — run: --run given logs one AUTO decisions.md line per successfully-applied action, under /backlog
- `tests/apply-refine-labels.test.js:245` — run: --run given logs one FAILED decisions.md line per failed action, under /backlog
- `tests/apply-refine-labels.test.js:338` — run: edit-only failure (no commentFile) still logs the same FAILED line shape as before #1073 (regression guard on #1072 behavior)
- `tests/apply-refine-labels.test.js:387` — run: a later non-empty --run after an earlier empty --run logs normally and never prints the empty-run note
- `tests/bin-lib/atomic-write.test.js:9` — writeFileAtomic: writes to a pid-suffixed tmp path in the same directory, then renames over the real path
- `tests/bin-lib/atomic-write.test.js:35` — writeFileAtomic: a write failure is cleaned up (best-effort unlink of the tmp file) and rethrown unchanged
- `tests/bin-lib/json-store.test.js:49` — writeJsonFile: two calls use distinct tmp paths within the same process (pid-suffixed, not a fixed name)
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/impact.test.js:334` — gitLocations: resolves a relative common dir against the cwd; null when git fails
- `tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/server.test.js:102` — resolveSafe rejects escapes and accepts in-tree paths
- `tests/friction-events-cli.test.js:72` — an explicit --worktree overrides deps.cwd()
- `tests/friction-events-cli.test.js:78` — excludes the primary run dir from the sibling lookup
- `tests/friction-events-cli.test.js:86` — success: primary events on stdout as a JSON array, tagged _source primary, exit 0
- `tests/friction-events-cli.test.js:103` — unions sibling (ad-hoc) run events with the primary run's, tagged _source adhoc
- `tests/friction-events-cli.test.js:485` — session id defaults to deps.sessionId() (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) and excludes the primary run
- `tests/hooks-context.test.js:855` — readRunStateWithParent: reads through the injected reader, and a throwing reader degrades to null
- `tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js:34` — report mode: lists uncovered reversals, writes nothing
- `tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js:47` — apply mode writes the revised body to --out
- `tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js:56` — apply mode with every reversal already noted writes nothing
- `tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js:64` — bundle run reads every spec-{id}/decisions.md and unions them
- `tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js:112` — an unreadable --summary-file or unwritable --out is exit 2

## Deliverables

- In each file, build every expected value and every fake-fs or fake-reader key with the same path operation the code applies: `path.resolve` where the code resolves, `path.join` where it joins. Define each fixture root once per file (for example `const REPO = path.resolve('/repo')`) and derive the rest from it.
- Leave a path the code passes through unresolved as a literal, as the skill row says.
- No `process.platform` branch and no `toPosix` on these values. They are native fs paths, not display IDs.
- Grep each file for every remaining POSIX absolute literal, not only the failing assertions (the skill's "fix only the named assertions" row).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: `node --test tests/apply-refine-labels.test.js tests/bin-lib/atomic-write.test.js tests/bin-lib/json-store.test.js tests/bin-lib/verify/impact.test.js tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/server.test.js tests/friction-events-cli.test.js tests/hooks-context.test.js tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js` passes on Linux with the same test count per file. No test is deleted or skipped.
2. AC2: discrimination is kept. In `tests/friction-events-cli.test.js` and `tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js`, swapping the fake reader's key back to an unreachable literal (`'/nowhere'`) makes the union and reversal tests fail on Linux, which proves the fakes are actually read.
3. AC3: a `windows-regression.yml` dispatch on the branch shows these 8 files with 0 failures of this class and no newly failing file.

## Release Note

No user-visible change: fixes Windows-only failures in tests that hard-code POSIX absolute fixture paths.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `tests/apply-refine-labels.test.js` — resolved run-dir expectations
- `tests/bin-lib/atomic-write.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/json-store.test.js` — joined tmp-path prefixes
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/impact.test.js` — resolved `commonDir` expectation
- `tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/server.test.js` — resolved `resolveSafe` expectation
- `tests/friction-events-cli.test.js` — resolved literals and fake `readEvents` keys
- `tests/hooks-context.test.js` — joined run path
- `tests/revise-pr-summary-cli.test.js` — fake fs keyed through `path.join`

groups.body:
Origin: #2767 class split — classification of windows-regression run 40169646104 (main 6a41ebe3a)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #2767, #2783, #1782

## Current State

`logWindowsLongpathsEvent` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js:367`) writes to `ctx.ownedRun.dir` whenever that field is set. The ad-hoc stamp in the same file (`stampAdHocRunDir`, line 289) first checks `ctxLib.isTrustedOwnedRun(ctx.ownedRun)`, because "a 'fallback' guess does not count (#2783)". The breadcrumb writer has no such check, so an EnterWorktree in a checkout that holds an unrelated run dir writes the `windows-longpaths` event into that unrelated run. `checkWindowsLongpaths` (line 373) runs only when `ctx.platform || process.platform` is `win32` (line 375). On Linux CI this path never runs in the end-to-end repro.

`tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js:21` is #2783's own repro. It asserts that the run resolved at EnterWorktree is the `fallback` guess, which is the unrelated sibling run (line 31). It passes that run as `ctx.ownedRun` to `post.run` with no `platform` (lines 33-37). On Windows it fails at line 64 with `nothing may land in the unrelated sibling run`.

`logWorktreeStalenessEvent` (line 350) has the same unguarded shape.

1 test in 1 file fails on Windows (line numbers as of 988cc584d).

### Failing tests

- `tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js:21` — #2783 repro: the harness refusal from an ad-hoc EnterWorktree session survives ExitWorktree remove

## Deliverables

- Route both breadcrumb writers, `logWindowsLongpathsEvent` and `logWorktreeStalenessEvent`, through one helper. The helper appends only when `ctxLib.isTrustedOwnedRun(ctx.ownedRun)` is true. A `fallback` guess gets nothing.
- Keep #1782's breadcrumb for a run that is actually owned. Any non-`fallback` attribution (`context.js:771`) still receives the `windows-longpaths` event.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: `node --test tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js tests/hooks-post-tool-use-worktree-staleness.test.js` passes on Linux.
2. AC2: a Linux-runnable win32 repro through the existing `ctx.platform` seam. The roundtrip test's `post.run` call carries `platform: 'win32'`, so Linux CI covers the Windows path. It fails before the fix and passes after.
3. AC3: unit pins in `tests/hooks-post-tool-use-worktree-staleness.test.js` with `platform: 'win32'`. With a `fallback` `ownedRun`, no `events.jsonl` is created in that dir. With a `session` `ownedRun`, exactly one `windows-longpaths` event lands there.
4. AC4: go-red. Removing the trust check from the helper fails AC2 and AC3's fallback case.
5. AC5: a `windows-regression.yml` dispatch on the branch shows `tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js` with 0 failures of this class and no newly failing file.

## Release Note

Windows: the `core.longpaths` breadcrumb no longer lands in an unrelated pipeline run's `events.jsonl` after an ad-hoc EnterWorktree.

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the event that landed in the sibling run on the Windows run was `windows-longpaths`. The log shows only the assertion message. The inference is that `checkWindowsLongpaths` is the only win32-only writer on this path. AC2 confirms or refutes it on Linux before any fix.
- `stampAdHocRunDir` does not update `ctx.ownedRun`. Whether the freshly minted ad-hoc dir should receive the breadcrumb is a build-time decision. This record only requires that a fallback guess never does.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js` — one trust-gated breadcrumb helper used by both writers
- `tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js` — `platform: 'win32'` on the repro's `post.run` call
- `tests/hooks-post-tool-use-worktree-staleness.test.js` — fallback and session ownership pins

groups.body:
Origin: #2767 class split — classification of windows-regression run 40169646104 (main 6a41ebe3a)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #2767, #4146 (this record takes its G part), #4134 (owns the test-impact tracer half of class G, the NODE_OPTIONS `--require` splice, including #4254), #3517, #3599

## Current State

Shipped skill prose splices `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` into JavaScript source. The shell expands it inside `node -e "…"` strings and inside unquoted `node-eval-file.js` heredoc bodies, so it lands in a JS string literal. There, `\a`, `\_` and `\c` are eaten as escapes and `\u` is a SyntaxError. A Windows root such as `D:\a\claude-tweaks\…` therefore reaches `require` as `D:aclaude-tweaks…`. The failing evidence is `Cannot find module 'D:aclaude-tweaksclaude-tweaksplugin/bin/lib/issues/grant-maturation.js'`.

How far it reaches: `grep -rhoE "require\(['\"]\\$\{?CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT" plugin/skills` finds 244 occurrences across 61 files. There are also non-`require` literals: `const path = '${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/CHANGELOG.md'` (`plugin/skills/init/bootstrap/version-check.md:58`) and `fs.readFileSync('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}…` (`plugin/skills/init/update-mode.md:64`). The failing tests run these sites:

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/grant-maturation-gate.md:32`, `:79`
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md:28`, `:56`, `:86`
- `plugin/skills/backlog/attention-mode.md:42`, `:58`, `:120`

Some snippets already pass values as data, for example `plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md:192` and `plugin/skills/wrap-up/refused-proposals.md:16`, which read `process.argv[1]`. Five suites work around the splice by forward-slashing the root inside the test (`tests/dispatch-mcp-timestamp-alias.test.js:60-62` and four siblings), which hides the production shape.

`tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js:483` also splices native temp paths for the `$ST_*` variables. Production prints those with `/` on win32 (`plugin/bin/session-tmp-resolve.js:26-27`, `formatPrintedPath`), so that half is test-only.

3 tests in 1 file fail on Windows (line numbers as of 988cc584d). The 18 failing `tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js` tests in the same class come from a different splice, NODE_OPTIONS `--require "<native path>"`. They are handed to #4134.

### Failing tests

- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js:283` — grant maturation snippet in dispatch/grant-maturation-gate.md runs: a NONE pending-grant marker is skipped with a note, a MEMBER one counts
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js:283` — grant maturation snippet in wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md runs: a NONE pending-grant marker is skipped with a note, a MEMBER one counts
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js:483` — attention-mode.md merge script runs: a forged newer NONE proposal is skipped with a note, the MEMBER one is read

## Deliverables

- Remove every JS-literal splice of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` from `plugin/skills/**`. Pass the root as an argument after the script and read it from `process.argv`: `require(require('path').join(process.argv[1], 'bin/lib/x.js'))`. A `node-eval-file.js` heredoc body reads it from its own argv. Paths stay native, and nothing respells the plugin root.
- Add a conformance suite that scans `plugin/skills/**/*.md` for `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` inside a quoted JS literal, in a `node -e` body or a `NODE_EVAL_EOF` heredoc. Give it a go-red self-test.
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` passes the root to each snippet as argv. Its `$ST_*` stand-ins use the form `formatPrintedPath` prints.
- Drop the forward-slash workarounds in the five suites that carry them, so they run with a native root.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: `node --test tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js tests/node-eval-file-heredoc-syntax.test.js` and the new conformance suite pass on Linux. The full `npm test` also passes, because skill prose is pinned by many suites.
2. AC2: a Linux-runnable proof of the Windows shape. A temp symlink whose name holds backslashes (`x\a\_temp`, a legal POSIX file name) points at `plugin/`. With that path as the root, each snippet `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` runs passes.
3. AC3: go-red for AC2. Running one snippet in its pre-change splice form with the same root fails with `Cannot find module`.
4. AC4: the conformance scan reports 0 splices, and its self-test flags a doctored `require('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/x.js')`.
5. AC5: a `windows-regression.yml` dispatch on the branch shows `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` with 0 failures of this class (its jq-CRLF failures belong to #3995) and no newly failing file.

## Release Note

Windows: skill steps that load plugin modules through `node -e` no longer fail with `Cannot find module` when the plugin is installed under a backslash path.

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: Claude Code on Windows exposes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` to a skill's Bash commands as a native backslash path. If it already uses forward slashes, the prose change is still correct but has no user-visible effect, and the test fixes are needed either way.
- `node-eval-file.js` (lines 23-28) forbids any `$` in a heredoc body other than `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. Once the root moves to argv, the delimiter can be quoted (`<<'NODE_EVAL_EOF'`). Check each body for other expansions before quoting it.
- Conformance suites extract these snippets by anchored fence text (`snippetBody` in `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js`, line 255). Run the full suite.
- 61 prose files make a large diff. Consider splitting it into sub-issues by skill directory, with the conformance suite landing last.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/**/*.md` (61 files) — the root passed as argv instead of spliced into JS
- `tests/plugin-root-splice-conformance.test.js` — new scan plus go-red self-test
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` — snippets run with a native or backslash-named root through argv
- `tests/dispatch-mcp-timestamp-alias.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-near-dup-pairs-script.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-named-target-exclusion-fixture.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js`, `tests/release-run-dir-lifecycle-conformance.test.js` — forward-slash workarounds dropped

Origin: reflect light from #4173

## Current State

Two skill files still carry the shape `tests/session-tmp-root-migration.test.js` forbids — a literal, unscoped `/tmp/{prefix}-{placeholder}.{ext}` scratch path that two concurrent sessions sharing an `{n}`/`{issue}` would overwrite — and neither is in that suite's `MIGRATED_FILES` list, so the suite never reads them (it scans only the listed files; #4065 and #4173 each added one more file to the list after a hand-found hit). Running the suite's own `LITERAL_TMP_RE` over every `plugin/skills/**/*.md` file during #4173's wrap-up matched exactly these two files and no other:

- `plugin/skills/flow/polish-execution.md` — `/tmp/polish-suggestion-{n}.md` (the polish `staged_suggestions` body handed to `bin/stage-item.js --file`)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief.md` — `/tmp/verification-brief-{issue}.md`, `/tmp/pr-brief-{issue}.md`, `/tmp/pr-timing-{issue}.md` (the Verification Brief and timing comment bodies posted with `--body-file`)

The same scan does not see shell-variable-shaped paths such as `/tmp/claim-${ISSUE}.md` (`_shared/issue-claims.md`) or `/tmp/assess-failure-comments-${N}.json` (`assess-agent-autonomy/failure-check.md`), because `LITERAL_TMP_RE` only tolerates `{placeholder}` tokens, so those are outside this record's verified scope; a builder should widen the regex or list them separately rather than assume they are clean.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Resolve each path above through `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/session-tmp-resolve.js" KEY=name-{n}.ext` and substitute the printed literal, exactly as `_shared/pr-run-comments.md` (#4065) and `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 2.5 (#4173) do.
- [ ] Add `flow/polish-execution.md` and `wrap-up/verification-brief.md` to `MIGRATED_FILES` and extend `_shared/session-tmp-root.md`'s consumer list.
- [ ] Add one whole-tree pin to `tests/session-tmp-root-migration.test.js` that applies `LITERAL_TMP_RE` to every `plugin/skills/**/*.md` file with a short, commented exemption list, so the next unmigrated file fails the suite instead of waiting for a hand-found incident.

- Running `LITERAL_TMP_RE` over every `plugin/skills/**/*.md` file reports no match outside the pin's exemption list (before this record it matches the two files named above — seen to match first).
- The new whole-tree pin fails when a literal `/tmp/polish-suggestion-{n}.md` is reintroduced into `flow/polish-execution.md` (revert-verified).
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief.md` — session-scope the brief and timing body paths

## Current State

- `releaseClaimedThisRun` (`plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js`, around lines 206-233) reads each target's blob fresh and tombstones whatever non-absent blob it gets back. It never classifies the blob or checks that its `runId` is this run's.
- #2329 routes the unverified target through it (`stopOrSkip(..., releaseThisIssue = true)`). An unverified write is exactly the case where the blob may be a competing run's live claim (this run's write lost the race), so the abort path can tombstone another run's live claim.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/issue-claims.md`'s Post-write verification paragraph says the release fires only when the fresh read "confirms it as this run's own live claim". Code and contract disagree.
- Raised by the Task 1 implementer of #4183 and confirmed by reading the function there; the file was outside that docs-only build's diff.

## Deliverables

- [ ] In `releaseClaimedThisRun`, classify the fresh blob (`classifyClaimBlob`) and tombstone it only when it is live under this run's `runId`; otherwise leave it untouched and name it in `releaseFailed` with an error that says it is not this run's claim.
- [ ] Decide and document what the abort path reports when the fresh read shows a competing live claim (the contract is silent on that case) in `plugin/skills/_shared/issue-claims.md` and `plugin/skills/flow/claim-targets.md`.
- [ ] Add tests in the claim-targets suite for: own live claim released, competing live claim left untouched, absent blob, and unreadable blob.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test where the fresh read returns a blob live under a different `runId` asserts no tombstone write happens and the issue appears in `releaseFailed`.
- A test where the fresh read returns this run's own live blob asserts it is tombstoned and listed in `released`.
- The all-or-abort release of the other confirmed targets is unchanged.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

A run that fails to verify its own claim no longer risks releasing another session's live claim.

## Technical Approach

- `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js` — modify
- `plugin/skills/_shared/issue-claims.md` — modify

Origin: ledger resolve gate (run 2026-10-25T090732-record-4210, refs #4210; items 11, 14, 15, 16)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

#4210 teaches the Bash gate parsers to track `"$( … )"` / `"${ … }"` / backtick nesting so a quoted `>` is never read as a redirect. Two separate walkers do it today: `advanceNesting` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` (the redirect scan) and the `subs` stack in `scanHeredocs` (heredoc stripping). Each re-derives shell quoting for its own purpose, and the heuristics still disagree with bash in four shapes, found by #4210's review and wrap-up:

- An unmatched closer inside `"$( … )"` (`case a)` patterns, a bare `}`) closes the nesting early and names a junk target: `echo "$(case $x in a) echo "p>q";; esac)"` resolves `/r/q;; esac)` (main resolved nothing). Fails closed (a false deny).
- An unquoted-delimiter heredoc inside `"$( … )"` whose body holds both `$(` and an apostrophe keeps its body visible, so the `'` leaves the nesting open and a later genuine redirect resolves nothing: `git commit -m "$(cat <<EOF\nDon't $(date)\nEOF\n)" && echo y > o.js`. Fails open.
- An unquoted `echo $(cmd x>y)` resolves the target `y)` (the group closer stays in the name). Pre-existing on main.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Replace the two nesting walkers with one shared word-lexer that understands `$( … )` (including `case` patterns and heredoc bodies), `${ … }`, backticks, and quote state, and have both the redirect scan and `stripHeredocBodies` read it.
- [ ] Make the four shapes above resolve as bash does, keeping the never-fabricate posture: ambiguity resolves to no target.
- [ ] Pin each shape in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` and the prefilter differential corpus in `tests/hooks-bash-prefilter.test.js`, and run the old and new parsers over a shared command corpus, accounting for every changed result.

## Acceptance Criteria

`fileWriteTargets('echo "$(case $x in a) echo "p>q";; esac)"', cwd)` resolves nothing, and `fileWriteTargets("git commit -m \"$(cat <<EOF\nDon't $(date)\nEOF\n)\" && echo y > o.js", cwd)` resolves `o.js`.
`fileWriteTargets('echo $(cmd x>y)', cwd)` resolves `y`, not `y)`.
`npm test` and `npm run test:perf` pass, and the `hooks-prefilter` perf budget holds.

## Release Note

The worktree-always gate reads nested command substitutions the way bash does, so fewer harmless commands are denied and no write slips past it.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — one shared nesting lexer for advanceNesting and scanHeredocs
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — pin the four shapes
- `tests/hooks-bash-prefilter.test.js` — add the shapes to the differential corpus

Origin: ledger resolve gate (run 2026-10-24T200414-record-4015, refs #4015)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s `redirectWriteTargets` reads one target per operator token. A chained redirect such as `echo a>b>c` (glued, from #4015) or `2>/dev/null>x` (start-anchored, from #3080) is one token, so the scan resolves the single joined name `b>c`. Bash writes both `b` and `c`.

The gate verdict for the joined name is not always the verdict for the real targets: it depends on the mix of absolute and relative parts, so the claim that the verdict is unchanged is not universally true. #4015's final whole-branch review asked for a follow-up record with corrected wording.

Telling which `>` inside a token is bare needs the same per-span quote record that the quoted-word glued redirect follow-up adds to `tokenize` (a quoted `>` such as `a>"b>c"` is data), so this lands after or with that change.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Split the target of a bare (unquoted) token at each further `>`, `>>` or `>|` and resolve every piece, for the glued and the start-anchored forms.
- [ ] Keep a quoted `>` in the target data: `echo a>"b>c"` resolves the one file `b>c`.
- [ ] Correct the wording in `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` and `docs/journeys/write-a-glued-redirect-from-the-main-checkout-4015.md` that lists chained redirects as a known gap.

## Acceptance Criteria

`fileWriteTargets('echo a>b>c', '/r')` returns the two targets `/r/b` and `/r/c`, and `fileWriteTargets('cmd 2>/dev/null>x', '/r')` returns `/r/x` only; `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` pins both and goes red when the change is reverted.

`fileWriteTargets('echo a>"b>c"', '/r')` returns the single target `/r/b>c`.

## Release Note

The worktree-always gate now sees every target of a chained redirect (`echo a>b>c`), not one joined name.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — `redirectWriteTargets` splits a bare token at further operators
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — pin the chained shapes

Origin: wrap-up Review Console, run 2026-10-17T100123-spec-3368-3365/spec-3365: confirmed finding plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md:28

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

**Related:** #3878, #3813, #4431, #3256, #3396, #3721, #3873, #3963, #3974, #3976, #3982, #3995, #4244, #4246, #4275, #4292, #4294, #4309, #4310, #4433, #4448, #4471, #4492, #4499, #4587

## Current State

Ruling R1 (`plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md:73`; `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js:177-184`, `closingRecords`) decides which records a run may close. It allows only records read from materialized headers, the `headers`/`worktree-headers` rungs. On a `manifest`/`worktree-manifest` rung `closingRecords` returns `[]` on purpose: manifest ids include specs that failed or never ran, which must get `Refs`, never `Fixes`. On the `unavailable` rung (no records resolved at all) it also returns `[]`. So an empty array means two different things, and the readers cannot tell them apart.

Three readers treat "empty" as "fall back to this run's Phase 1 identified record":

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md:28-34`, the current-branch commit's `Fixes #{issue}` lines. It uses `inputs.closingRecords` "when non-empty", otherwise the Phase 1 record. On a manifest rung that stamps `Fixes #N` for a record R1 excluded, and GitHub closes it once the commit reaches the default branch. In a multi-spec current-branch run, that can be a spec that failed or never ran. This is the confirmed finding; it still holds on `main` as of 2026-10-30.
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md:122`, the `issues` key of `verify-expectations.json`. Same "non-empty, else Phase 1" rule, so verify expects that record to close.
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js:442-452` `resolvedIssueNumbers`. When `closingRecords` comes back empty, it falls through to those expectations.

Only `cleanup-procedures-execution.md`'s Section C step 2 bash distinguishes the cases. It falls back to the worktree-mirror glob only when the field is not an array (`if(!Array.isArray(c))process.exit(1)`).

`tests/wrap-up-record-resolution-conformance.test.js`'s `assertNoGateRestatement` forbids any reader from naming `sources.records`, `worktree-headers` or `HEADER_SOURCES` outside Section C's one definition sentence. So the fix cannot be a prose condition on the source rung; the distinction has to come from the pack.

**Decision (human-approved 2026-10-30):** `closingRecords` carries R1's decision explicitly:

- an array, possibly empty, when records resolved: this is the set the run may close;
- `null` when no records resolved at all (`unavailable`): the run has no decision, and only then may a reader fall back to the Phase 1 record.

## Deliverables

1. `pack.js`'s `closingRecords({ records, source })` returns `null` on the `unavailable` rung and keeps today's results on the other rungs: `records` on a header rung, `[]` on a manifest rung. Update its comment and the pack's documented field shape. The wrap-up pack conformance docs name `closingRecords` as array-or-null.
2. `execution-and-verification.md`'s current-branch `Fixes` sentence:
   - an array, even an empty one, is the set to stamp;
   - only a `null` field or a pack that could not be produced falls back to the Phase 1 record;
   - an empty array stamps no `Fixes` line.

   It cites Section C step 2 and never names the source rungs.
3. `review-console.md` step 11's `issues` sourcing follows the same rule.
4. `engine-verify.js`'s `resolvedIssueNumbers` returns `closingRecords` whenever it is an array, empty included. It falls through to `verify-expectations.json` only when the value is `null`.
5. Update the pin at `tests/wrap-up-record-resolution-conformance.test.js:102` and add the cases below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `closingRecords({ records: [41, 42], source: 'manifest' })` returns `[]`, `closingRecords({ records: [], source: 'unavailable' })` returns `null`, and the header rungs return their records (`tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js`).
- `resolvedIssueNumbers` on a manifest-rung fixture whose `verify-expectations.json` lists `issues: [41]` returns `[]`. On an `unavailable` fixture with the same file it returns `[41]` (`tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js`).
- A prose test pins two things in `execution-and-verification.md` and `review-console.md` step 11: an empty `closingRecords` stamps or records nothing, and only a `null` field or a missing pack falls back to the Phase 1 record.
- `assertNoGateRestatement` still passes for both files: neither names a source rung.
- Revert each change and show which new test fails (the pack function, `engine-verify.js`, and each prose sentence).
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

A current-branch wrap-up no longer closes the issue of a spec that failed or never ran in a multi-spec run.

## Technical Approach

Keep R1 in one place. The pack already decides it; the bug is that its "no decision" and "decided: none" outputs look the same. `null` versus `[]` gives readers the distinction without restating the rule, which is what the conformance test enforces. Section C's existing bash already treats a non-array as fall-back, so it needs no change. Confirm that with a test fixture rather than by reading.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `closingRecords` returns `null` on the `unavailable` rung
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` — `resolvedIssueNumbers` honours an empty array
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — current-branch `Fixes` sentence
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` — step 11 `issues` sourcing
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — read only: Section C step 2 is the definition the readers cite
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js` — rung cases
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` — manifest versus unavailable fallthrough
- `tests/wrap-up-record-resolution-conformance.test.js` — updated pin and new prose cases
- `tests/wrap-up-pack-conformance.test.js` — field shape, if it pins `closingRecords` as an array

## Gotchas

- `dispatch/two-call-gate.md` and `wrap-up/cleanup-procedures.md` item 4 also read `inputs.closingRecords`. Both already treat an empty result as "nothing to stamp", so they need no change. Check them anyway, and name them in the PR.
- The pack is produced and read within one run by one plugin version, so a `null` field does not reach an older reader.

Surface: backend

**Related:** #3915, #3706, #2713, #3396, #3813, #3847, #3901, #3902, #3903, #3976, #4081, #4084, #4107, #4197, #4252, #4388

## Current State

When a retry run adopts a worktree whose branch already exists on `origin`, `build/adopted-branch-collision-check.md` asks `findPriorAttemptPr` (`plugin/bin/lib/worktree/remote-branch-collision.js:150-167`) whether the foreign remote tip is this record's own failed earlier attempt. On a match (state `prior-attempt`), the build runs `git merge --no-edit {remoteSha}` and `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` Step 1 reopens and rebinds that PR. It never stops.

Today a PR qualifies as an earlier attempt when all of the following hold:

- it is CLOSED;
- it comes from the same repository (`isCrossRepository === false`);
- its body's first line carries the `claude-tweaks-run:` marker;
- it closes one of the run's records (`prClosesIssue === true`);
- its head is an ancestor of origin's tip.

None of those checks tells a dispatch failure tombstone apart from a PR a human closed to reject the approach. Both are closed, run-marked, same-repo PRs that close the record, and on this repo both closes come from the same OWNER account. The next retry silently adopts the rejected branch, merges any commits pushed after the close, reopens the PR, and builds on top of the work the human turned down. Review lens `3b` reported this at line 163 (run `2026-10-21T215830-record-3887`), and the tiebreak confirmed it on `e71e18563`. It still holds on `origin/main` as of 2026-10-26.

The legitimate prior-attempt shape comes from exactly one producer, `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` Step 6 step 5. In that one settle step it:

1. posts a fresh `Attempt {N} failed: …` comment on the **issue** (`attemptFailedCommentBody`, `plugin/bin/lib/issues/retry.js`; matched by `countFailedAttempts`'s `ATTEMPT_RE`);
2. find-or-creates a `<!-- run-comment: failure -->` pointer comment on the PR;
3. runs `gh pr close`.

A human rejection close has no fresh `Attempt N failed` issue comment immediately before it.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `findPriorAttemptPr` requires failure-tombstone evidence before a PR qualifies. The record's issue must carry a trusted (`isTrustedComment`, `plugin/bin/lib/issues/comment-trust.js`) `Attempt {N} failed` comment created no more than `TOMBSTONE_CLOSE_WINDOW_MS` before the PR's `closedAt`, and not after it. A PR without that evidence stays `foreign`, so the build falls through to item 4's stop card and a human decides.
- [ ] `findPrsForBranch` fetches `closedAt` for each PR. The evidence lookup reads the record issue's comments, at most once per record per check. A failed or partial lookup yields no match: the branch stays `foreign`, which fails closed, as every other doubt in this function already does.
- [ ] `build/adopted-branch-collision-check.md`'s item 5 prose and its embedded snippet are updated to state the new condition. They keep naming dispatch's failure path as the only producer of the `prior-attempt` shape.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/bin-lib/worktree/remote-branch-collision.test.js` cover four cases:
  - a tombstone PR (attempt comment just before `closedAt`) still matches;
  - a PR with no attempt comment stays foreign;
  - a PR whose only attempt comment is older than the window stays foreign. This is the stale-marker case: an earlier failure, then a retry that reopened the PR, then a human closed it;
  - a failed issue-comment lookup stays foreign.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A same-repo, run-marked, CLOSED PR that closes the record and whose head is an ancestor of origin's tip, but has no trusted `Attempt N failed` issue comment within the window before its `closedAt`, makes `findPriorAttemptPr` return `null`. The adopted-branch check then reports `foreign` with the stop card.
- [ ] The tombstone shape that `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` Step 6 step 5 leaves still returns `{ number, url }`, so a dispatch retry still adopts its own failed attempt with no stop.
- [ ] An `Attempt N failed` comment from an untrusted author (`authorAssociation` not OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR) never counts as evidence.
- [ ] Each of the four new test cases fails when the evidence check is removed from `findPriorAttemptPr`, and the suites `tests/bin-lib/worktree/remote-branch-collision.test.js`, `tests/adopted-branch-collision-snippet-fixture.test.js` and `tests/adopted-branch-collision-prose-conformance.test.js` pass.

## Release Note

Stop a dispatch retry from adopting the branch of a pull request you closed yourself — it now stops and asks instead of building on rejected work.

## Technical Approach

Add the tombstone check inside `findPriorAttemptPr`'s loop, after the existing `prClosesIssue` and ancestry checks. Each candidate PR needs its `closedAt`, which comes from the same `gh pr list` call as long as `findPrsForBranch` asks for it. It also needs the comments of the record the PR closes. Inject an issue-comment reader alongside `git`, the way `gh` is injected today, so tests stay hermetic, and read through `gh issue view {n} --json comments` or `gh api`. Evidence is an `ATTEMPT_RE` match (export it from `retry.js` instead of copying the regex) on a comment that `isTrustedComment` accepts and whose `createdAt` falls in `[closedAt - TOMBSTONE_CLOSE_WINDOW_MS, closedAt]`.

The window value is the builder's call. Settle posts the issue comment, then the PR pointer, then closes, all in one step, so a few minutes is ample. 15 minutes is a reasonable default. Make it an exported module constant, not a policy key.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/worktree/remote-branch-collision.js` — `findPriorAttemptPr` gains the tombstone-evidence check and an injected comment reader; `findPrsForBranch` adds `closedAt` to its `--json` fields
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/retry.js` — export `ATTEMPT_RE` for reuse
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/comment-trust.js` — read only (`isTrustedComment`)
- `plugin/skills/build/adopted-branch-collision-check.md` — item 5 prose and the snippet state the new condition
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — read only, the producer whose Step 6 step 5 order the window relies on
- `tests/bin-lib/worktree/remote-branch-collision.test.js` — the four new cases
- `tests/adopted-branch-collision-snippet-fixture.test.js` — keep green against the updated snippet
- `tests/adopted-branch-collision-prose-conformance.test.js` — keep green against the updated item 5 prose

## Gotchas

- Post-close commits stay adoptable on a genuine tombstone (my call). The ancestry check (head is an ancestor of origin's tip, not equal to it) was a deliberate choice in #3887 (Review Focus 1). Once a human-closed PR no longer qualifies, the only commits merged are ones pushed to a dispatch-tombstoned branch, which is someone contributing to the retry, not rejected work.
- Older tombstones from before #1963 put attempt comments only on the PR, not on the issue, so they no longer qualify and stop with the `foreign` card. That is the intended fail-closed direction. Don't widen the evidence to PR comments to rescue them, because the PR's `run-comment: failure` pointer is updated in place and its timestamp is not reliable.
- With `gh` absent there is already no PR lookup (item 5 notes this; #3915 tracks an MCP-fed one), so nothing changes there.
- Author association does not tell bot and human apart on this repo, since both act as OWNER. Timing against the fresh attempt comment is the discriminator, and the trust check only stops a third party from planting one.

Origin: reflect full from #3947

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

A skill step that dispatches agents or calls CLIs is specified in prose, and nothing at spec, plan or authoring time asks what happens when each of those calls fails.

In #3947 (Step 3.7, `plugin/skills/review/step3-tiebreak.md`), the SDD final review needed 1 Critical and 6 Important fixes, and the later 4-lens review found 23 more findings. Most of them were the same kind of gap: what the reviewer does when a dispatch fails or returns non-DONE, when `write-findings` exits 2, when `resolve-tiebreak` crashes, or when `log-decision.js` fails. Each was added after the fact, across fix commits a2d09600d, a645f740b, cc098dd27 and 494bb6045.

`docs/skill-authoring.md` and `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` have no rule or check that asks for a failure path per external call.

## Deliverables

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` gains a rule: a step whose prose dispatches an agent or runs a CLI states, for each such call, its next move on failure (retry once / fallback rung / surface and stop) and the log line it writes.
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` gains a check: a plan task that adds or changes such a step carries a failure-path table (call → failure mode → next move → log line) before its prose is written.
- A conformance test pins both texts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/skill-authoring.md` contains the failure-path rule and names the three next-move kinds.
2. `plan-authoring-checks.md` contains the failure-path table check and its trigger (a task touching a step that dispatches an agent or runs a CLI).
3. A test asserts both, and it was shown to go red without each text.

## Release Note

Skill steps that dispatch agents or run tools now have to say up front what happens when each call fails, so those gaps are found while planning instead of in review.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — add the failure-path rule
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — add the failure-path table check

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2724 (auto-filed structurally-stuck tracker, kept), #3898 (release runs are owned there)

## Overview

Run directories pile up because nothing closes a run whose session died. Measured 2026-10-22: 78 empty `-adhoc-standalone` directories (0 staged items and 0 decision lines in every one), and 27 stale formal runs (20 open PRs, 6 closed-unmerged, 1 merged). A session that crashes never fires SessionEnd, so its run stays `active` forever. The SessionStart "unfinished runs" banner shows 3 only because `MAX_REPORTED = 3` caps it with no overflow line, and it has no liveness filter: it listed three runs that sibling sessions were probably still driving.

This record is the report-only half of the fix. It adds a pure disposition function (run shape by liveness verdict gives close, leave, or orphan, with a reason), runs it inside reconcile in report-only mode so reconcile says what it would close and closes nothing, narrows the SessionStart banner to dead-and-orphaned runs with an overflow line, and makes a session archive its own ad hoc run at SessionEnd. Closing for real is a later record that must ship in a release after this one, so every consumer project gets a dry run on its own pile first.

The asymmetry the maintainer agreed on governs every rule here: settle findings aggressively, close runs conservatively. Closing a run a live sibling session is still driving ends that run's enforcement and event logging invisibly. A run left open by mistake costs one more banner line.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 8

## Non-Goals

- Reconcile closes nothing in this record. No `run-state.json` is flipped to `clean` by the new rows, no staged item is dropped, no directory is archived by them. Turning that on, and `close-run --abandon`, are #3978.
- Reconcile gains no GitHub write and no skill-file write, and never carries out a staged item's outcome. It never deletes a branch, removes a worktree, or changes claim labels.
- No filing of backlog records per orphaned run, and no listing of live sibling runs "for information"; both relocate the noise.
- No change to the existing merged, `orphaned-mint`, `adhoc-superseded`, and `abandoned-interrupted` archive paths beyond the `live` skip; replacing `abandoned-interrupted`'s recency test is #3979.
- Release runs (`-release-standalone`) closing at their own end is #3898's scope; this record only covers dead ones through the standalone row.
- Not the auto-filed structurally-stuck tracker (#2724), which stays as it is.

## Prerequisites

| Spec | Title | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| #3973 | Add a run-liveness verdict module and an owner block in run-state.json | must merge first: this record consumes `runLiveness` |
| #3845 | A nested `claude -p` inside a pipeline session marks the parent's run interrupted at its SessionEnd | in progress; it also edits `session-end.js` and writes a false `interrupted` this record must tolerate |

## Current State

- `classifyRunDir(ctx, now)` in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` (line 1602) walks `CLASSIFY_ORDER = ['orphaned-mint', 'abandoned-interrupted', 'adhoc-superseded', 'merged', 'structurally-stuck']`. `adhoc-superseded` requires an ad hoc mint whose worktree is gone and a directory idle for `ADHOC_SUPERSEDED_TTL_MS` (30 days). `abandoned-interrupted` requires `status: interrupted` and no owner-attributed event within `STALE_INTERRUPTED_TTL_MS` (24 hours); `orphaned-mint` requires a directory with no `config.yml` idle for `ORPHAN_MINT_TTL_MS` (24 hours).
- `collectStaleRuns(cwd, { cache, exclude, pluginRoot })` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-residue.js` (line 56) walks `iterRunDirsWithState`, skips ad hoc directories (`isAdHocRunDir`), and stops at `MAX_REPORTED = 3` (line 36) with no overflow line. Its sibling `CONSOLE_OVERFLOW_LINE` (line 201) is the existing overflow pattern: `- … more run(s) may have unreviewed console items (newest 3 shown).`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` renders the banner; line 148 carries the instruction text "Say with it that only the session owning a run should close it: a listed run may be live in a sibling session right now, ...", the warning this record drops.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-end.js` stamps `{ status: 'interrupted', lastEvent: 'session-end' }` onto the session's own non-`fallback` run, then appends a `session-end` event.
- Staged items live in the run's `staged/` (and `spec-*/staged/`); `listStagedItems` and `hasStagedItems` are in `archive-merged.js` (lines 443 and 461). Kinds are classified by `classifyStagedItem(filename, text, siblingText)` in `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` (line 179); review findings are the `review-unconfirmed-` and `review-contested-`/`review-debate-` prefixes (`SECTION_MAP`, line 47).
- Reconcile writes its results to `.claude-tweaks/reconcile-cache.json` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js`, `CACHE_FILENAME`) and renders them through `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/format-summary.js`'s `CATEGORIES` table (line 50).
- `#3973` provides `runLiveness(runDir, { now, probes }) -> { verdict: 'live' | 'dead' | 'unknown', evidence }` and the `owner` block in `run-state.json`.
- Tests: `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` (classifier fixtures), `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` (banner), `tests/reconcile.test.js`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] A pure disposition function, `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/disposition.js` (next to the verdict module), taking run shape, liveness verdict, PR state, branch and worktree facts, and staged inventory, and returning `{ action: 'close' | 'leave' | 'orphan', reason, evidence, dropFindings }` and exporting the set of reasons that return `close` as `CLOSE_REASONS`. The ordered rules below are its contract, evaluated first match wins with a default of `leave`.
- [ ] A facts gatherer next to it (`plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/facts.js`, injectable git and `gh` runners) that produces the inputs the function needs and maps any failed probe to the "cannot determine" value (never to a value that closes): `pr` is `merged | closed-unmerged | open | none | unknown`; `branch` is `{ localExists, remoteExists, uniqueCommits }` where `uniqueCommits` is a count against the integration branch's merge-base or `null` when it cannot be computed; `worktree` is `{ exists, dirty }` with `dirty` `null` when `git status` fails. `pr: 'unknown'` (a `gh`-absent environment, an API error, or the SessionStart fast path) and any `null` fact yield `leave` for every new row.
- [ ] The `live` skip: no archive path, existing ones included, acts on a run whose verdict is `live`. The skip is one guard at the top of the per-run loop in `archiveMerged`, which computes the verdict once per run and hands it to `classifyRunDir` as `ctx.liveness` (the classifier stays pure); a run directory with no `run-state.json` yields `unknown`. The existing merged, `orphaned-mint`, and `adhoc-superseded` paths gain only this skip and keep acting on `unknown`, each having its own evidence (a merged PR, a mint that never wrote `config.yml`, a worktree gone for 30 days). The existing `abandoned-interrupted` path also gains the skip; its own 24 hour recency test stays, and it keeps acting on `unknown`, until #3979 replaces it with the verdict.
- [ ] Reconcile evaluates the disposition for every non-clean run in REPORT-ONLY mode, behind one module constant `RUN_AUTO_CLOSE_REPORT_ONLY = true` in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` read at exactly one call site: it writes `would close {run} ({reason}, evidence ...)` lines to its summary and to `reconcile-cache.json` (`wouldClose`), lists the `orphan` runs in the same cache (`orphaned`, each with its PR number and reason) and in the archive check's `--json` output, reports a count of `unknown` runs in the summary (never in the banner), and closes nothing. Each pass records `reportOnlyPassAt` in `reconcile-cache.json`, the marker #3978 reads so that auto-close never acts on a checkout that has not first had a report-only pass. The summary renders wherever reconcile's summary already renders; a false positive is reported through `/claude-tweaks:feedback`.
- [ ] Banner: `collectStaleRuns` lists only runs that are `dead` and orphaned, newest run id first, keeps the 3-row cap, and adds an overflow line in the style of `CONSOLE_OVERFLOW_LINE`: `- … and {N} more orphaned run(s) (newest {MAX_REPORTED} shown): node "{root}/bin/hooks.js" reconcile --dry-run --json --checks archive`. The banner stays network-free: it reads the `orphaned` list from `reconcile-cache.json`, re-checks each entry's verdict offline with `runLiveness`, drops an entry that is no longer `dead`, and lists nothing for a run absent from the cache (nothing is listed before the first reconcile pass). Each row names its reason and a resume command, using the existing integrity-derived line text where it applies (the shipped-unclosed and consolidated-pass lines are kept as the text of rows that pass the filter). The "only the owning session should close a run" instruction text in `session-start.js` is removed.
- [ ] `session-end.js` closes and archives its own ad hoc run directly instead of marking it `interrupted`, keeping `events.jsonl` in the archive for `/claude-tweaks:feedback`. Order: append the `session-end` event first, then `closeRunState` (recording `closedBy: 'session-end'`) and `archiveRunDir`, with no write to the run directory afterwards (a late write would recreate the archived directory). It applies only when the `reason` on the SessionEnd input is one after which the session cannot continue (not `clear`, not `resume`) and when `staged/` is empty or holds only review findings; otherwise today's `interrupted` stamp is kept.
- [ ] `docs/reconcile-checks.md` documents the disposition table and the report-only switch; the switch is a release step, not a policy key.
- [ ] Review this repository's report-only output by hand before the enabling record; record the result in the PR body. Pass criterion: every `would close` line on a formal run names a run the maintainer agrees is abandoned; any disagreement blocks the enabling record until the disposition is fixed. The 27 stale formal runs measured on 2026-10-22 (20 open PRs, 6 closed-unmerged, 1 merged) are the review set; the 20 open-PR runs are `orphan` by design and the banner stays loud for them until their PR merges or closes or a human runs the abandon command.

The disposition rules, in order, first match wins, default `leave` ("staged ok" means `staged/` and every `spec-*/staged/` is empty or holds only review findings; "other staged" means any other kind):

| # | Run shape | Conditions | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | any | verdict `live` | `leave`; never touched by any archive path |
| 2 | any | verdict `unknown` | `leave` for the new rows; existing paths keep acting on `unknown` |
| 3 | `-adhoc-standalone` | verdict `dead`, staged ok | `close` (no 30-day wait); `events.jsonl` moves with it |
| 4 | `-adhoc-standalone` | verdict `dead`, other staged | `orphan`, reason `staged items need an outcome` |
| 5 | other standalone (`-tidy-`, `-sweep-`, `-release-standalone`) | verdict `dead`, `staged/` empty | `close` |
| 6 | other standalone | verdict `dead`, `staged/` not empty | `leave` (the existing staged-proposals banner and #3898 own it) |
| 7 | formal | PR merged | `leave` here; the existing merged path acts, unchanged |
| 8 | formal | verdict `dead`, PR closed unmerged, staged ok | `close`, reason `pr-closed-unmerged`, `dropFindings` set |
| 9 | formal | verdict `dead`, PR closed unmerged, other staged | `orphan`, reason `staged items need an outcome` |
| 10 | formal | verdict `dead`, PR open (draft or ready) | `orphan`, reason `draft PR #N, session gone` or `PR #N open, session gone`; never closed |
| 11 | formal | verdict `dead`, no PR, (`uniqueCommits` greater than 0 or worktree dirty) | `orphan`, reason `unpushed commits on {branch}` or `uncommitted changes in {worktree}` |
| 12 | formal | verdict `dead`, no PR, (branch absent locally and on origin, or `uniqueCommits` 0), (worktree absent or clean), no owner-attributed event for 24 hours, staged ok | `close`, reason `nothing-to-resume`, `dropFindings` set |
| 13 | formal | verdict `dead`, no PR, otherwise as row 12 but other staged | `orphan`, reason `staged items need an outcome` |
| 14 | any | anything else (including any `unknown` fact: `pr: 'unknown'`, `uniqueCommits: null`, `dirty: null`) | `leave` |

Row 12's 24 hour floor is the existing `abandoned-interrupted` window (`STALE_INTERRUPTED_TTL_MS`) reused so a just-started or just-paused run is never closable sooner than today; the design table does not state it, and it only narrows what can close.

Staged items: for rows 8 and 12, review findings (the `review-unconfirmed-`, `review-contested-`, `review-debate-` kinds) would be dropped with reason `run-abandoned`, which report-only mode lists in `dropFindings` but does not do. Any other staged kind (reflect, queue write, skill update, `shadow-dup-*`) makes a run not closable and orphaned, as rows 4, 9 and 13 say. `run-abandoned` is introduced here as report vocabulary and registered in `_shared/auto-decision-log.md` by #3978, where the drop becomes real.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A fixture run whose owner PID is alive with a matching start time (a live-PID fixture) is never listed by the banner, never reported as `would close`, and is skipped by the merged, `orphaned-mint`, `adhoc-superseded`, and `abandoned-interrupted` paths; one test per path. The first three still act on an `unknown` fixture.
2. Each numbered rule of the disposition table has a test asserting its `action` and `reason`, including the default row; a run with verdict `unknown` yields `leave` for every new row, and `pr: 'unknown'`, `uniqueCommits: null`, and `dirty: null` each yield `leave` even when every other fact says close (a `gh`-absent fixture does not close a run whose PR was never seen).
3. Fail-open variants of the disposition function (treating verdict `unknown` as `dead`, and treating `pr: 'unknown'` as `none`) are present as injected faults and the corresponding tests fail against each.
   a. A falsely `interrupted` run (status `interrupted`, owner PID alive with a matching start time, as #3845 produces) is `live`: not listed, not `would close`, and left by the `abandoned-interrupted` path.
   b. The report-only constant is read at one call site (a source-scan test finds exactly one); with the constant set, the act path is unreachable (a test calling it with the constant true observes no write).
4. A reconcile run over a fixture containing a dead ad hoc run, a dead closed-unmerged-PR run, and a dead no-PR run with nothing to resume writes three `would close` lines to the summary and to `reconcile-cache.json`, and leaves every `run-state.json`, `staged/`, and directory byte-identical (a test snapshots the tree before and after).
5. A dead formal run with an open draft PR, and one with unique commits and no PR, yield `orphan`, appear in the banner, and are not in the `would close` lines.
6. A dead run holding a non-review staged item (for example `reflect-1.md`) yields `orphan` with reason `staged items need an outcome`; a dead closed-unmerged-PR run holding only `review-unconfirmed-*` items yields a `would close` line that also lists the findings it would drop with reason `run-abandoned`, and drops none.
7. With five dead orphaned runs in `reconcile-cache.json` the banner prints the newest three rows and one overflow line naming the remaining count (2) and the listing command; with three or fewer it prints no overflow line. With only `live`, `unknown`, or would-close runs, or with no cache, the banner prints nothing about runs. A cached orphan whose verdict is now `live` is dropped.
8. Each banner row names its reason (for example `draft PR #N, session gone`, `unpushed commits on {branch}`, `staged items need an outcome`) and a resume command; the text "only the session owning a run should close it" no longer appears in `session-start.js` (a grep test pins this).
9. `session-end.js`, given a session whose own run is ad hoc and a terminal SessionEnd reason, closes the run (status `clean`, `closedBy: 'session-end'`) and archives the directory including `events.jsonl`, with the `session-end` event appended before the archive and no write afterwards (the archived directory is not recreated); given a non-terminal reason (`clear`, `resume`), or an ad hoc run holding a non-review staged item, it stamps `interrupted` exactly as before; given a formal run it still stamps `interrupted` exactly as before; given a `fallback` attribution it touches nothing.
   a. The set of terminal reasons is taken from the SessionEnd `reason` values the harness actually emits (see the Gotchas probe), and the test enumerates each.
10. `docs/reconcile-checks.md` states that the new rows are report-only in this release and that the switch is deleted by the record that enables closing.

## Release Note

Added a dry-run report of runs that could be closed automatically, trimmed the unfinished-runs banner to runs that really need attention, and made sessions archive their own scratch run when they end.

## Technical Approach

The disposition function is pure (no I/O): reconcile gathers the facts (PR state from the existing merged-proof path, branch and worktree facts, staged inventory, the verdict from `runLiveness`) and passes them in, so the table is tested without a filesystem. Report-only is one module constant read at the single call site that would act, so the enabling record is a one-line flip plus deleting the constant.

The banner reuses the same disposition: it lists exactly the runs whose action is `orphan` and whose verdict is `dead`. A `would close` run is not listed in the banner (it is reconcile's to report) and is not closed in this release.

### Data / API Surface

`disposition({ shape, verdict, pr, branch, worktree, staged })` returns `{ action, reason, evidence, dropFindings: string[] }`, where `shape` is one of `adhoc`, `standalone`, `formal`; `pr` is `merged | closed-unmerged | open | none`; `dropFindings` lists staged files that would be dropped with reason `run-abandoned`. Reconcile's summary gains a `would-close` category (`format-summary.js`'s `CATEGORIES`) and `reconcile-cache.json` gains a `wouldClose` list of `{ runDir, reason, evidence }`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/disposition.js` — new, the pure disposition function
- `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/index.js` — `runLiveness`, consumed (created by #3973)
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `live` skip in `classifyRunDir`'s callers and the report-only evaluation
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/format-summary.js` — `would-close` summary category
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js` — `wouldClose` persisted in `reconcile-cache.json`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-residue.js` — `collectStaleRuns` filter, overflow line
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` — banner render, removal of the owning-session warning text
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-end.js` — close-and-archive of the session's own ad hoc run
- `docs/reconcile-checks.md` — disposition table and report-only switch

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the resume command each banner row prints actually re-enters the run. Existing re-entry text in `collectStaleRuns` covers the shipped-unclosed and consolidated-pass cases; for `draft PR, session gone` and `unpushed commits` confirm what `/claude-tweaks:flow` adoption (`flow/preflight.js`'s `computeAdoption`) accepts before wording the command.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the SessionEnd `reason` values the harness emits (for example `clear`, `resume`, and the exit reasons) and which of them leave the session running; probe it from a real hook invocation and record the raw values in the PR body before fixing the terminal set. Until verified, treat any reason other than a clearly terminal one as non-terminal.
- Reconcile must never act on `unknown`, and a probe error is `unknown`, never `dead`; do not add a shortcut that treats a missing `owner` block as dead (the legacy 72 hour route in `runLiveness` is the only legacy path to `dead`).
- The SessionEnd ad hoc close is safe only because the run is the ending session's own and ad hoc runs never resume (a resumed session mints a fresh one). Keep the `fallback`-attribution guard that `session-end.js` already has: a guessed run is never closed.
- Nested `claude -p` sessions (#3845) can fire SessionEnd against the parent's run. The ad hoc direct close must be gated on the same own-run attribution as the existing stamp, never on `ctx.runDir`.
- Report-only means no write of any kind to a run directory by the new rows: no `closedBy`, no `decisions.md` line, no archive move. The only writes are the summary and `reconcile-cache.json`.
- `reconcile` runs on a fast path at SessionStart (`FAST_CHECKS`) and a background path; the disposition needs PR state, which may require `gh`. Respect the existing gh-absent posture (`_shared/github-write-transport.md`'s MCP path and the accepted MCP gap documented in `docs/reconcile-checks.md`): without PR state a formal run is `leave`, not `close`.
- The banner currently skips ad hoc runs (`isAdHocRunDir`) so they cannot crowd out a real interrupted run; keep that skip for ad hoc and listing only `orphan` rows keeps the cap meaningful.
- File overlap with open records: `archive-merged.js` with #3975 (same file, sequential), #3945, #3740, and #3721; `session-residue.js` with #3950; `session-end.js` with #3845. Related: #2724 (the structurally-stuck tracker stays) and #3898 (release runs close at their own end there).
- Skill edges, if any, go in `docs/skill-graph.md` only; new reconcile checks follow `docs/reconcile-checks.md`'s "Adding a new check" registration list, including the `reconcile-threw` fallback duplicate in `hooks.js`.
