groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3721 (same `archiveRunDir` commit code; build sequentially), #3855 (superseded by this project)

## Overview

When a run's gitignored half has been archived but its git-tracked `work/{N}-spec.md` header (or `spec-{N}/work/`) is still live, the directory is in the "split state" of #3855. Measured on 2026-10-22: 254 local live directories hold only a tracked spec header with an archive twin, and 258 of the 264 tracked live run directories on `origin/main` have a twin. Reconcile never reports them, because `iterRunDirsWithState` skips a directory whose archive twin is clean. The completion command reconcile would emit for that state (`hooks.js archive-run --run`) also always fails, because `archive-run` refuses a directory with no `run-state.json`. And `archiveRunDir` has a latent hazard in the same code path: when it stages only twin resolutions and no `workMoves`, it runs `git commit -m ... --` with no paths, which commits the whole staged index.

This record makes the split state visible, ships a command that can actually complete it, fixes the commit hazard, and runs the command once on this repository. Every consumer project on pr-first has the same pile, so the command ships in the plugin rather than as a maintainer-only script.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 7

## Non-Goals

- No change to where new runs' headers end up; moving the header on the run branch before merge is #3976. This record cleans what already exists and reports what recurs.
- No dual-path reader work (#3974).
- Not a general run-directory janitor. The CLI handles live directories that hold only tracked `work/` (or `spec-*/work/`), nothing else.
- No change to `archive-run`'s refusal of directories with no `run-state.json`; `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` pins that refusal and it stays.
- No archive retention or pruning of `archive/` itself.

## Prerequisites

| Spec | Title | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| #3721 | archive-run: commits the archive move on the current branch without reporting the commit or its branch | open; edits the same `archiveRunDir` commit code, so build the two sequentially |

## Current State

- `iterRunDirsWithState` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` line 225) skips a live directory when `readRunState(archive/{name})` reports `status: 'clean'`. A directory with no `run-state.json` of its own passes the earlier `wantClean` test, then falls to that skip.
- `isArchivedPendingTrackedMove(root, dir)` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` line 798) detects the split state: the archive twin exists and every live entry is a git-tracked `work/` or `spec-{n}/work/`. `archivedPendingTrackedMoveCommand(dir)` (line 831) returns `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hooks.js" archive-run --run "<dir>"`. Under `worktree-always: true` the sweep skips with reason `archived-pending-tracked-move` and that command; without it the sweep completes the archival in-process.
- `archiveRunDir` (line 1014) stages `twinPlan` resolutions and `workMoves`, then commits with `commitPaths = workMoves.flatMap(([src, dest]) => [src, dest])` (line 1301). When `workMoves` is empty and only `twinPlan` is non-empty, `commitPaths` is empty and the call is `git commit -m "[reconcile] archive run <id>" --`, which commits the whole index (#2241 scoped the commit for the `workMoves` case only).
- `plugin/bin/sweep-stray-run-dirs.js` is a one-time sweep (#593) that already moves tracked `work/` subtrees into `archive/{run-id}/` through `archiveRunDir`, folds `events.jsonl` into an existing twin, and commits once per directory. It has `--root`, `--dry-run`, and `--log`.
- `housekeeping-auto-merge` is a policy key (`plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js`, `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema.md` row 141) derived from `autonomy` (`true` at `trusted`/`unattended`), consumed by tidy Step 7.5 and wrap-up's `residue-sweep.md` to auto-arm a housekeeping PR.
- Reconcile check registration is documented in `docs/reconcile-checks.md` ("Adding a new check", line 37); the split-state skip reasons are in its "Archive skip reasons and residue pruning (#1892)" section (line 127).
- Tests: `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` has the split-state tests at lines 3685 to 3935 (the `worktree-always` skip at 3898 and the in-process completion at 3922); `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` line 71 pins the no-`run-state.json` refusal.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `iterRunDirsWithState` gains an opt-in option (for example `includeTrackedShells: true`) under which the clean-twin skip no longer hides a live directory that holds only tracked `work/` or `spec-*/work/`; reconcile's archive check passes it and reports each such directory as `archived-pending-tracked-move`. The default behavior is unchanged, so `resolveRun`'s fallback scan and `session-start.js`'s unfinished-run report keep not seeing the shells.
- [ ] New shipped CLI `plugin/bin/archive-tracked-shells.js` (name may change at build): moves every such shell to `archive/{run-id}/`, or deletes the live copy when an identical archived copy is already tracked; enumerates the shells read-only in the main checkout (a shell is a live directory that holds only tracked `work/` or `spec-*/work/` and whose archive twin's `run-state.json` is `clean`; that clean twin is the definition of a finished run), then does the moves in a scratch worktree cut from `origin/main` (`_shared/scratch-worktree.md`) on a fresh branch, comparing against the tracked archived copy; opens one batched housekeeping PR for every shell found; never commits on the main checkout; honors the `housekeeping-auto-merge` policy key (read from the main checkout's `policy.yml` through `resolve-policy.js`; the key's derived default applies when unset) for whether that PR is armed. Reuses `sweep-stray-run-dirs.js`'s mechanics rather than reimplementing the move.
- [ ] Reconcile prints that command (not `archive-run`) as the `archived-pending-tracked-move` completion under `worktree-always`; without `worktree-always` it performs the same move in place, as `archiveRunDir` does today.Resolved by the maintainer (2026-10-22): without worktree-always, reconcile completes at most one shell in place per reconcile pass; any larger batch is delegated to the shipped CLI's single housekeeping PR, so the pile is never mass-committed in place on whatever branch is checked out.
- [ ] `archiveRunDir`'s commit passes an explicit pathspec in every case, including the twin-only case.
- [ ] List the CLI in `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s CLI listing and update `docs/reconcile-checks.md`'s skip-reason section for the new completion command. The CLI is a standalone bin run by a human or by a session following reconcile's printed command; it is not a reconcile check and needs none of that file's check-registration sites.
- [ ] One-time: run the CLI on this repository. About 258 tracked live directories on `origin/main` have an archive twin; the roughly 6 without one are not touched by the CLI (they have no clean twin to prove a finished run); the CLI lists them in its envelope as `untwinned`, and they are classified individually by hand in the same PR (archive, keep, or delete, each with a reason in the PR body).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `node plugin/bin/hooks.js reconcile --dry-run --json --checks archive`, run against a fixture whose archive twin carries a clean `run-state.json` and whose live directory holds only tracked `work/`, lists that directory with reason `archived-pending-tracked-move`. Run before the change, the same fixture lists nothing (the test is red against the old iterator).
2. The command reconcile emits for that state succeeds in a test fixture under `worktree-always: true`: it exits 0, creates a branch, moves the shell to `archive/{run-id}/`, opens one PR (the `gh` runner is injected and asserted), and makes no commit on the main checkout's branch (`git rev-parse HEAD` on the main checkout is unchanged).
3. With three shells in the fixture the CLI opens exactly one PR and the branch carries every move; a re-run after the PR is simulated merged is a no-op that exits 0 with `moved` empty. A re-run while the first PR is still open reuses the deterministic branch `housekeeping/archive-tracked-shells` and the open PR (printing its URL) rather than opening a second one, and a re-run after a crash partway through resumes from the branch's current state.
4. A shell whose archive twin is byte-identical is deleted rather than moved; a shell whose twin differs is left in place and named in the output with the differing path (the same `compareWorkTwin` rule `archiveRunDir` applies, which compares file bytes; the delete path never uses a looser comparison). The PR still opens for the shells that were clean, and the CLI exits 1 to flag the left-behind ones.
5. With `housekeeping-auto-merge` resolving `true` the CLI arms the PR with `gh pr merge --auto --squash`; resolving `false` it leaves the PR unarmed and says so in its output. A rejected arming call (for example a repository with no branch protection) leaves the PR unarmed and reports the rejection; it is not an error exit.
6. A test calls `archiveRunDir` in the twin-only case (empty `workMoves`, non-empty `twinPlan`) with an unrelated file staged in the index, and asserts that file is not in the resulting commit and that the recorded `git commit` argv ends with an explicit, non-empty pathspec. Run against the old code the test fails.
7. The CLI honors `--dry-run` and makes no change and no PR. With `--no-pr` it makes the branch and commits locally, pushes nothing, and prints the branch name. In a `local-merge` project, or where `gh` is absent, it refuses with exit 2 and a message naming `--no-pr`, unless `--no-pr` was given. A failure after the scratch worktree exists removes the worktree and leaves no half-built branch on the remote.
8. `docs/plugin-structure.md` lists the CLI with its flags and `docs/reconcile-checks.md`'s skip-reason section names it as the `archived-pending-tracked-move` completion; the existing docs conformance tests pass.
9. Build-time check: the housekeeping PR opened for this repository contains a move or delete for every shell the CLI's dry run lists, and its body classifies each of the roughly 6 `untwinned` directories. Post-merge check: `git ls-tree origin/main .claude-tweaks/pipelines/` lists no live tracked directory that has a clean archive twin; directories classified "keep" in the PR body are the only exceptions.
10. The default `iterRunDirsWithState` call (no option) still skips a live shell whose twin is clean, so `session-start.js`'s unfinished-run report and `resolveRun`'s fallback scan list none of the shells; a test per caller pins this.

## Release Note

Added a command that archives stranded run spec headers through one housekeeping pull request, and made reconcile report them instead of ignoring them.

## Technical Approach

Keep the move itself in `archiveRunDir` (git mv, `compareWorkTwin`, `resolveIdenticalWorkTwin`) and have the CLI orchestrate: enumerate shells with `isArchivedPendingTrackedMove`, create a fresh branch in a scratch worktree, run `archiveRunDir` for each, then push and open one PR. The in-process path (no `worktree-always`) and the CLI differ only in where the commit lands.

### Data / API Surface

`archive-tracked-shells.js [--root <dir>] [--dry-run] [--no-pr]`: prints one JSON envelope `{ moved: [...], deleted: [...], conflicts: [...], untwinned: [...], pr: { number, url, armed } | null }` and exits 0 on success (including nothing to do), 2 on a malformed call or an unsupported environment, and 1 when any shell was left because its twin differs. Reconcile prints one line for the whole batch, `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/archive-tracked-shells.js" --root "<root>"`, rather than one command per directory.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `iterRunDirsWithState` clean-twin skip
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `isArchivedPendingTrackedMove`, `archivedPendingTrackedMoveCommand`, `archiveRunDir` commit pathspec
- `plugin/bin/archive-tracked-shells.js` — new CLI
- `plugin/bin/sweep-stray-run-dirs.js` — mechanics to reuse (and the CLI listed in `docs/plugin-structure.md`)
- `docs/reconcile-checks.md` — registration and the skip-reason table
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — split-state fixtures and the pathspec regression test
- `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` — refusal that must stay pinned

## Gotchas

- The existing split-state tests pass because they create the archive twin as an empty directory with no `run-state.json`; the real 258 cases have a twin with a clean `run-state.json`. Build the new fixtures with the real shape, or the regression will not reproduce.
- The skip in `iterRunDirsWithState` serves other callers too (`resolveRun`'s fallback scan, `session-start.js`'s unfinished-run report). That is why the new behavior is an opt-in option passed only by reconcile's archive check, not a change to the default (a default flip would list about 254 shells as unfinished runs in every SessionStart banner).
- `archive-run` refuses a directory with no `run-state.json`, naming `archiveOrphanedMint`; do not weaken that refusal, because the CLI is the supported path for this shape.
- Under `worktree-always`, nothing may be committed on the main checkout: do the work in a scratch branch and worktree (`_shared/scratch-worktree.md`), and never `git stash`.
- Memory note: `archive-run` commits the whole staged index, so run `git status` and assert a clean index before the CLI starts, and commit with explicit pathspecs.
- Batching is deliberate: one PR for every shell found, not one per directory, so the housekeeping pass does not itself produce a pile of PRs. `housekeeping-auto-merge` decides arming only; it never bypasses the merge-verification gate.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the CLI can rely on `archiveRunDir(root, runDir)` committing per directory on the scratch branch with a result it can read (its current contract). #3721 is changing that commit and its reporting; after rebasing on #3721, re-pin the assumed return shape with a test.
- The twin's non-`work/` content (`run-state.json`) is gitignored and exists only in the main checkout, which is why enumeration runs there and the moves run in the scratch worktree against the tracked archived `work/`.
- The first reconcile after this ships will see the whole pile and print the CLI command once; run the one-time housekeeping PR before relying on a quiet reconcile summary.
- Cited line numbers are as of 2026-10-22; find the code by symbol (`iterRunDirsWithState`, `isArchivedPendingTrackedMove`, `archiveRunDir`, `commitPaths`) and the tests by name.
- Related: #3855 (this record implements its second and third deliverables). #3721 edits the same commit code; build sequentially and rebase on it.
- File overlap with in-progress and open records: `archive-merged.js` with #3945, #3740, and #3721; `context.js` with #3845, #3836, #3811, and #3736. Rebase before opening the PR.
- Windows: the CLI shells out to `git` and `gh`; apply the `windows-checkout-test-parity` skill to any path assertion and use the injectable runner seam for the PR step (`gh-api-module-pattern` skill).

groups.title: Report stranded spec-shell dirs, ship a command that archives them via one PR, and stop archiveRunDir committing the whole index

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Overview

A run's materialized spec header (`work/{N}-spec.md`, or `spec-{N}/work/{N}-spec.md` for a multi-spec parent) is committed on the run branch on purpose, and six readers depend on finding it at the live run-dir path `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run-id}/`. The cutover record in this project (#3976) moves that header to `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/{run-id}/` on the run branch just before merge, so a merged pr-first run leaves no live tracked directory on `main` (#3855, option a). That move is only safe once every reader can find the header at either location.

This record is the expand step, before any move happens. It adds one shared resolver that returns a run's header location at the live path or the archived path, on the filesystem and inside a git tree, and migrates all six readers onto it. No file moves; behavior for every run that exists today is unchanged.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 7

## Non-Goals

- No `git mv` of any header and no wrap-up change; that is #3976, which is blocked by this record.
- No `.gitignore` change.
- No change to `materialize.md`'s contract text; it changes when the move lands.
- No new reader beyond the six named, and no reader restating the dual-path rule after this record: each calls the resolver.

## Prerequisites

None. This record is a pure expand step and can be built first.

## Current State

The six readers, each with its own copy of the live-path assumption:

- `plugin/bin/verify-run-bookends.js` — `isSpecCommitted` (line 140 region) probes `git cat-file -e HEAD:<rel>` over `specCandidatePaths(runDir, issue, multiTarget)`; this is the gh-absent materialize check cloud runs depend on.
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` — `specOnBranch` (line 120) lists `git ls-tree <branch> -- <rel>/work/` and then `-r <rel>/` for the multi-spec shape, matching `/(^|\/)(spec-\d+\/)?work\/\d+-spec\.md$/`.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — `hasMaterializeCommit` (line 1191) runs `git log {integration}..HEAD -- <run>/work` plus the `spec-*/work/*` pathspec; its result arms the bookkeeping-stamps gate (IL-131). `getMaterializedRecordNumbers` (line 1389) reads the same headers.
- `plugin/bin/lib/pr-bookkeeping/precondition.js` — returns `not-materialized-yet` (line 80) when `hasMaterializeCommit` is false.
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `resolveRecords` (line 226) and `closingRecords` (line 182) read `path.join(runDir, 'work')` first, then the worktree mirror, then `manifest.yml`; the result decides `Fixes #N` in the PR body.
- `plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.js` — `hasMaterializedHeader` (line 105) reads `work/{n}-spec.md` and `spec-{n}/work/{n}-spec.md` under the run dir and its worktree mirror (`headerBases`), and a header whose `record:` line names another number does not count.

There is no shared module for "where is this run's header". The closest existing helpers are `perSpecPathspec` and `toPosix` in `pre-tool-use.js` and `specCandidatePaths` in `verify-run-bookends.js`, which are local to those files.

The archived layout is already produced today by `archiveRunDir` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`, line 1014): `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/{run-id}/work/...` and `.../archive/{run-id}/spec-{N}/work/...`.

Tests: `tests/hooks-bookkeeping-stamps-gate.test.js`, `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`, and the existing suites for `verify-run-bookends`, `flow-preflight`, `pr-bookkeeping`, `wrap-up/pack`, and the dispatch first-call check.

## Deliverables

- [ ] New `plugin/bin/lib/run-header.js` exporting the resolver functions in Data / API Surface below. They resolve a header at the live path (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run-id}/work/{N}-spec.md` or `.../spec-{N}/work/{N}-spec.md`) or the archived path (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/{run-id}/work/{N}-spec.md` or `.../archive/{run-id}/spec-{N}/work/{N}-spec.md`), on the filesystem and as candidate paths and pathspecs for git-tree readers. The archived path can be written by two writers, the wrap-up move in #3976 and `archiveRunDir`; the resolver treats a header found at the archived path as the run's header whichever wrote it.
- [ ] Migrate `verify-run-bookends.js` to the resolver.
- [ ] Migrate `lib/flow/preflight.js` `specOnBranch` to the resolver.
- [ ] Migrate `pre-tool-use.js` `hasMaterializeCommit` and `getMaterializedRecordNumbers` to the resolver, so the `git log {integration}..HEAD` range also matches a commit that touched only the archived path. The only deny gate that consumes `hasMaterializeCommit` is `checkBookkeepingStampsGate` (`pre-tool-use.js` line 1742); the only other consumer is `precondition.js`. Re-run `grep -rn hasMaterializeCommit plugin/bin` at build and record the consumer list in the PR body.
- [ ] Migrate `lib/pr-bookkeeping/precondition.js` to the resolver (through `hasMaterializeCommit`, with no second copy of the dual-path rule).
- [ ] Migrate `lib/wrap-up/pack.js` `resolveRecords` and `closingRecords` to the resolver.
- [ ] Migrate `lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.js` to the resolver.
- [ ] Tests: for each reader, a case where the header exists only at the archived path and the live path is absent, including the git-tree readers on a branch whose last commit moved the header; the existing live-path tests stay unchanged and green.
- [ ] A source-scan conformance test (`bin-source-scan-conformance` skill) pinning that no file under `plugin/bin` outside the resolver and the archive writers builds a header path itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For each of the six readers, a test with a fixture where the header exists only at `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/{run-id}/work/{N}-spec.md` (live path absent) gets the same answer the reader gives for the live-path fixture: materialized, the same record number, and the same `Fixes #N` decision in `pack.js`.
2. The same six tests pass for the multi-spec shape, with the header only at `.../archive/{run-id}/spec-{N}/work/{N}-spec.md`.
3. For the git-tree readers (`isSpecCommitted`, `specOnBranch`, `hasMaterializeCommit`), a test builds a real git repo whose branch's last commit is a `git mv` of the header from the live path to the archived path, and each reader reports materialized.
4. The `{integration}..HEAD` range bound (#1674) is not widened, in three fixtures: (a) a run that never materialized (no commit at either path) returns false; (b) run A's archived header is reachable from the integration branch and a worktree for run B inherits it, so `hasMaterializeCommit` for run B returns false; (c) run A's own branch, whose commits in the range include its materialize commit and the move commit, returns true.
5. `checkBookkeepingStampsGate` behaves identically for a branch whose only in-range commit touching the run is the archived-path move and for the same run materialized at the live path (the gate arms in both); the fixture lives in `tests/hooks-bookkeeping-stamps-gate.test.js`.
6. A run with a header at the live path behaves exactly as before: the full existing suites for the six readers pass without edits to their expectations.
7. Precedence is pinned: with the header at both locations (a stale live copy, or a mid-move state), a single-record lookup returns the live copy; if the live copy's `record:` line names another number the lookup falls through to the archived copy; with a live `work/` directory that lacks this record's header and the header archived, the lookup returns the archived header.
8. A conformance test (source scan with a stripped-comment reader and a floor on matched sites) asserts that none of the six reader files contains the path segment `'archive'` or the text `pipelines/archive`, and that no other file under `plugin/bin` builds a header path (a path join or template containing both `work` and `-spec.md`) outside `plugin/bin/lib/run-header.js` and the archive writers `lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` and `sweep-stray-run-dirs.js`. The grep `grep -rln "work.*-spec\.md" plugin/bin` run at build establishes that the six are the full reader set; its output goes in the PR body.
9. Failure postures are unchanged, one test per reader, with the current behavior captured before the change: `isSpecCommitted` and `specOnBranch` return `null` on a git error; `precondition.js` returns `materialize-check-failed`; `hasMaterializeCommit` and `getMaterializedRecordNumbers` return what they return today on a git failure (the test pins that value); the two filesystem readers (`pack.js`, `first-call-artifact-check.js`) treat an unreadable header as absent exactly as today. A git failure is never reported as "not materialized" by a git reader that did not report it before.

## Release Note

Changed spec-header checks to find a run's header at either its live or archived location, with no change to existing runs.

## Technical Approach

One resolver, imported by all six readers, so the dual-path rule exists in one place. The resolver takes the run id rather than a pre-joined path, because the archived path replaces the `{run-id}` parent segment (`pipelines/archive/{run-id}`), not just a tail. Every reader derives the run id as `path.basename(runDir)`; `archiveRunDir` names the archive directory after the same basename, so the two always agree.

For the git-tree readers the resolver returns an ordered pathspec list (live first, then archived) and the readers keep their own git invocation (`cat-file`, `ls-tree`, `log`), so each retains its own failure semantics. For the filesystem readers (`pack.js`, `first-call-artifact-check.js`) it takes an ordered list of base roots (the run dir's checkout root, then the worktree mirror's root, the same order those readers use today) and returns existing header files. Precedence is root by root: within a root, live before archived and flat `work/` before `spec-{N}/work/`. The resolver does no mirror discovery itself; the caller supplies the roots, which keeps the main-checkout anchoring rule (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`, IL-127) the caller's.

### Data / API Surface

`plugin/bin/lib/run-header.js`:

- `headerRelPaths(runId, recordNumber)` returns the ordered list of repo-relative POSIX paths for one record (live flat, live `spec-{N}`, archived flat, archived `spec-{N}`), for readers that need concrete paths (`git cat-file -e`).
- `headerPathspecs(runId)` returns the `git log` and `ls-tree` pathspecs covering `work` and `spec-*/work/*` at both locations, for readers that enumerate.
- `findHeaderFiles(roots, runId, recordNumber)` returns the existing header files for one record on the filesystem, in the precedence order above (the caller applies its own `record:` line check and falls through to the next file).
- `listHeaderDirs(roots, runId)` returns every existing header directory as `{ dir, location: 'live' | 'archived', specN: number | null }` for enumerating readers (`pack.js`, `getMaterializedRecordNumbers`); where one record appears in both locations, the earlier in precedence wins.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/run-header.js` — new shared resolver
- `plugin/bin/verify-run-bookends.js` — `isSpecCommitted`, `specCandidatePaths`
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` — `specOnBranch`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — `hasMaterializeCommit`, `getMaterializedRecordNumbers`, `perSpecPathspec`
- `plugin/bin/lib/pr-bookkeeping/precondition.js` — `not-materialized-yet` path
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `resolveRecords`, `closingRecords`, `headerEntries`
- `plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.js` — header probe and worktree mirror
- `tests/hooks-bookkeeping-stamps-gate.test.js` — materialize-commit gate fixtures
- `tests/run-header.test.js` — new suite for the resolver and the conformance grep

## Gotchas

- `git log` pathspecs: a wildcard directory component followed by a literal tail never matches. `spec-*/work` does not match; `spec-*/work/*` does (the comment in `hasMaterializeCommit` records this as empirically verified). Keep the trailing wildcard in the archived spec pathspec as well: `pipelines/archive/{run-id}/spec-*/work/*`.
- `hasMaterializeCommit` is range-bound to `{integration}..HEAD` so a merged run's materialize commit, inherited by later worktrees, does not arm the gate against runs that never materialized (#1674). After the move, the archived path is part of the squash on `main`, so the range bound must still exclude it for an unrelated run; AC 4(b) pins this. When the integration branch cannot be resolved the function falls back to the unbounded walk (documented in its own comment); the archived pathspecs inherit that fallback and the same over-arming risk, which this record does not change.
- The gh-absent cloud bookends check (`isSpecCommitted`) must keep passing after the move lands; it is the reason cloud parity depends on this record.
- `git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>` cannot glob; the resolver must hand it concrete candidate paths, not pathspecs.
- A run resumed after the move still has to read as materialized, so the dispatch first-call check must accept the archived location too.
- File overlap with open records: `pre-tool-use.js` with #3875 and #3847, `pack.js` with #3686. Rebase on `main` before opening the PR and re-run the affected suites.
- The dual-path rule is permanent, not a compatibility shim: while a run is in flight its header lives at the live path, and only at wrap-up does it move. There is no removal condition; the live candidates stay for as long as runs have a live phase.
- The filesystem readers keep the `record:` line check: a header at the archived path whose `record:` line names another number must not count either.
- Apply the `windows-checkout-test-parity` skill to the new path-matching tests (POSIX separators in git pathspecs, native separators on the filesystem side).
- Per the `pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions` skill, `hasMaterializeCommit` arms a deny gate; widening what counts as materialized widens what the gate sees, so check each deny gate that consumes it for an exemption-scope change; AC 5 pins the one gate that does.

groups.body:
**Related:** #3877
Origin: build of #3877 (final whole-branch review finding #6)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

After #3877, `/tidy`'s `## Arm ready PR` action (`plugin/skills/tidy/actions-github-issues.md`) holds a record-linked PR whose acceptance labeling never landed. That covers three cases: the run's `verify.json` `acceptance-labeling` row is not `pass`/`skip`, no `demo:pending` is set on its `Fixes` records, and no trusted brief/try-it run comment exists. In those cases the action logs a `SKIP` to `decisions.md` instead of arming.

`_shared/github-pr-scan.md`'s `repo-wide` item 9 still classifies that same PR as a granted `[pr-unarmed]` candidate on every sweep. So `tidy/step-6-auto.md` re-stages the same record-linked "Arm ready PR" row each run, and a human approves an arm that only holds again. `step-6-auto.md`'s own header treats a recurring staged item as a missing routing rule.

## Deliverables

- Item 9 (or tidy's Step 6 routing) applies the same acceptance-labeling landed check as the arm action. It reuses `dispatch/close-out.md` step 3's live-state precheck: `demo:pending` on every `Fixes` record, or a trusted brief/try-it run comment. Where a local run dir resolves, it also reads that run's `verify.json` `acceptance-labeling` row.
- A not-landed record-linked PR routes to **Yours**, carrying the paste-ready recommendation the arm action already names: `/claude-tweaks:dispatch close-out #{record}`, or the no-run-dir alternative. It does not appear as an Arm ready PR row.
- The arm action's own guard stays as the execution-time backstop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A record-linked unarmed PR whose labeling has not landed surfaces under Yours with `/claude-tweaks:dispatch close-out #{record}` (or the no-run-dir alternative), not as an Arm ready PR row.
2. A record-linked PR whose labeling has landed still stages as an Arm ready PR row.
3. Housekeeping-marker PRs are unaffected.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

`/tidy` no longer keeps offering to arm a PR it will only hold for missing acceptance labeling.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/github-pr-scan.md` — item 9 classifies a not-landed record-linked PR away from the Arm candidate set
- `plugin/skills/tidy/step-6-auto.md` — routes the not-landed record-linked flavor to Yours
- `plugin/skills/tidy/actions-github-issues.md` — arm guard stays as backstop; cross-reference the scan-time routing

**Related:** #3880
Origin: build final review of #3880

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

At the Wrap-Up Review Console, ratifying an `sdd-ruling-*` item (`apply`, per `wrap-up/review-console-appendix.md`'s `sdd-ruling-*` bullet) writes its ledger row to `accepted` and files nothing; only `reverse` composes a record proposal (`staged/ledger-record-sdd-ruling-{N}.md`). #3880 added a safe-deferral class that console-auto ratifies at `unattended`: `Defers: yes` with exactly one valid `Defer-reason:` header (including `tangential` and `pre-existing-outside-diff`). That deferred work ends as a terminal `accepted` row, the ledger is deleted once nothing is open, and the work reaches no backlog record. This contradicts CLAUDE.md's "No implicit deferrals" and `_shared/deferral-gate.md`'s premise that a `Defer-reason:` goes with a record. It is not a regression: before #3880 every ratified ruling was dropped the same way. Found by #3880's final whole-branch review (finding I-3). The ratify contract is shared by the single-run console (`review-console.md` step 1 and step 7), the multi-spec console (`flow/multispec-review-console.md`), the interactive Override vocabulary (`review-console-interactive.md`), the on-PR console (`_shared/console-on-pr.md`, `_shared/console-execution.md`, `bin/lib/reconcile/console-execute.js`), and `finish-console`.

## Deliverables

Ratifying a deferral ruling (`Defers: yes`, or any `Defer-reason:` header line, with a valid reason) composes a record proposal via `specShapedBody`, the same way `reverse` does today. Current State is the ruling and the finding it deferred; Deliverables is the deferred work; the record carries the staged file's own `Defer-reason:` value. The proposal routes through the console's record-creation step in the same pass. Once the record exists, the ledger row is written `deferred` with Resolution `ratified → #{n}`; if creation fails or is refused, the row stays `open`.

Ratifying a `Defers: no` ruling (a settled design decision) keeps today's `accepted` write-back unchanged.

Apply the same rule at every console surface that ratifies a ruling: single-run, multi-spec, interactive, on-PR/reconciler execution, and `finish-console`.

Add a conformance test pinning the ratify-files-a-record rule in `wrap-up/review-console-appendix.md` and its code twin, if one exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

Ratifying a `Defers: yes` `sdd-ruling-*` item with a valid `Defer-reason:` produces a backlog record carrying that reason, and the ledger row is `deferred` with the record number.

Ratifying a `Defers: no` ruling still writes the row `accepted` with no record.

A refused or failed record creation leaves the row `open`, never `accepted` or `deferred` without a record number.

`npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Ratifying a deferred SDD ruling at the Review Console now files the deferred work as a backlog record instead of closing it silently.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console-appendix.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/_shared/console-execution.md` — modify
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/console-execute.js` — modify

Surface: infra

Origin: reflect full from #3783
**Related:** #205, #3783, #3740, #3508, #3706, #3721, #3905, #3936, #3946, #3963, #3973, #3974, #3975, #3976, #3977, #3979, #3982

## Current State

`plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` treats `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` (the sub-issues a run is closing, which the parent gate counts as `CLOSED` while they are still open) as a prose contract. A table (around line 195) tells each sub-issue-side caller what to pass:

| Caller | Set it passes |
|---|---|
| wrap-up Phase 4 execution | the one sub-issue this run is closing |
| wrap-up auto-merge short-circuit | the one sub-issue this run is closing |
| dispatch group auto-merge gate (`settle-and-merge.md`) | every member of the group (the merge carries one `Fixes #{issue}` per record) |
| dispatch close-out step 3 (`close-out.md:77`) | the PR's `Fixes` record numbers |

Ruling #205 kept this as prose while three callers existed and set "a fourth sub-issue-side caller" as the revisit condition. #3783 (PR #3869) added the fourth (close-out step 3), and the file now defers the decision to this record. An omitted set defaults to `{the sub-issue in hand}`, so the silent-no-op mode is closed, but nothing checks a wrong non-empty set: a caller that passes the wrong records labels the wrong parent's gate.

Every row is a different description of one fact: the records the merge closes. Under `pr-first` that is the PR's `Fixes` lines, which GitHub reports as the PR's `closingIssuesReferences`. `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` already reads that field (around line 320). Under `local-merge`/`current-branch` it is the wrap-up pack's `inputs.closingRecords` (`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `closingRecords`), the same set the carrier commit's `Fixes` lines are composed from.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Ruling recorded in `verification-brief-parent-gate.md`: `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` is **derived, not passed**. A shared helper computes it from the merge's own closing references, and the per-caller table becomes a description of that derivation.
- [ ] A `plugin/bin/` CLI (e.g. `closing-set.js`) returns the set as JSON: `--pr {n}` reads the PR's `closingIssuesReferences` (reusing `archive-merged.js`'s fetch shape); `--run {dir}` reads `wrap-up-pack.json`'s `inputs.closingRecords` for a run with no PR. An unreadable source exits non-zero with a reason and never prints `[]` as if nothing closes.
- [ ] All four callers call it instead of composing the set by hand: wrap-up Phase 4 execution (`execution-and-verification.md`), the auto-merge short-circuit (`auto-merge-short-circuit.md`), dispatch's group gate (`settle-and-merge.md`), and dispatch close-out step 3 (`close-out.md`)
- [ ] On a helper failure, keep today's default of `{the sub-issue in hand}`, and log the failure so the degraded set is visible
- [ ] A gh-absent (MCP transport) path, per `.claude/skills/mcp-agent-fetch-node-compute`: the agent fetches the PR's closing references through MCP and the helper reads them from a JSON file

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests: a PR whose body closes `#1` and `#2` yields `[1, 2]`; a `--run` dir whose pack lists `[7]` yields `[7]`; a failed PR read and a missing pack each exit non-zero with a reason and print no set
- A conformance test asserts each of the four caller files invokes the helper and none composes `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` by hand
- `verification-brief-parent-gate.md` carries the new ruling, keeps the `{the sub-issue in hand}` default as the failure fallback, and no longer defers to this record
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Parent acceptance gates compute which sub-issues a merge closes the same way at every merge site.

## Technical Approach

The original question was a helper versus prose with a new revisit condition. The trade-off it named, a helper "adds a code path every caller threads through" while "prose leaves a wrong non-empty set uncaught", only favors prose if the helper merely takes what the caller hands it. A helper that **derives** the set from the merge's own closing references removes the wrong-value risk entirely: the set equals what GitHub (or the carrier commit) will close, which is the definition the table was approximating. That is what makes the threading cost worth paying, and it also covers a fifth caller by construction instead of by a table row it might misread.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/closing-set.js` — new CLI
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/closing-set.js` (or a sibling module) — derivation with an injectable runner
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — existing `closingIssuesReferences` read to reuse or extract
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `closingRecords` (local-merge source)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` — ruling and table
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — Acceptance labeling bullet
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md` — its `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` line (around line 110)
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — group gate
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md` — step 3
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — list the new CLI

## Gotchas

- The group gate labels **before** the merge lands, so `closingIssuesReferences` must be read from the open PR's body, not from a merged-PR event; confirm it is populated on an open draft PR whose body carries `Fixes #N` lines.
- `closingIssuesReferences` only lists same-repo issues linked by a closing keyword. A record the PR fixes without the keyword is not in the set, so that case keeps today's behavior: the gate sees it as still open.
- If extracting the shared read from `archive-merged.js`, follow `.claude/skills/shared-contract-extraction`'s migration discipline so reconcile's behavior is unchanged.

## Original request

Decide #205 revisit — shared helper for CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES now that four callers pass it

Origin: reflect full from #3783

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` keeps `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` (the sub-issues a run is closing, read by the Self-inclusion rule) as a prose contract: each sub-issue-side caller reads the table there and passes its own set. Ruling #205 kept it prose while three callers existed and said to revisit it as a real code change once a fourth caller was added.

#3783 (PR #3869) added that fourth caller: `dispatch/close-out.md` step 3 now runs `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 1 with `CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` = the PR's `Fixes` records when a parked PR's labeling never landed. The parent-gate file now records that the condition is met and defers the decision to this record.

Nothing checks the value a caller passes: a wrong non-empty set labels the wrong records, which the default-to-the-sub-issue-in-hand rule does not catch.

## Deliverables

- A decision, recorded in `verification-brief-parent-gate.md`, on whether the closing set moves into a shared helper (for example a function that derives it from a PR's `Fixes` lines or a dispatch group) or stays a prose table.
- If a helper: every sub-issue-side caller (wrap-up Phase 4 execution, the auto-merge short-circuit, dispatch's group gate, dispatch close-out step 3) calls it, and a test pins each caller's use.
- If prose: the ruling states the new revisit condition.

## Open Question

Should `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` become a shared helper now that four callers pass it, or stay a prose table with a new revisit condition? A helper adds a code path every caller threads through; prose leaves a wrong non-empty set uncaught.

## Release Note

Parent acceptance gates compute which sub-issues a merge closes the same way at every merge site.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` — record the #205 revisit decision
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md` — fourth caller passing CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES

groups.body:
Surface: infra

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3809
**Related:** #3973, #3736, #3744, #3822, #3876, #3900, #3915, #3974, #3975, #3978, #3979, #3983, #3989

## Current State

`plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's **Resolve now** bullet (line 127) carries a multi-run chase. A conflict resolution during a multi-run `local-merge` reconciliation ends in a `git commit`, and E1 (`runInner`'s tail loop in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`) checks every commit against `ctx.runDir`, the newest non-terminal run in the project regardless of owner (`docs/hooks.md`'s "Two resolutions, not one"). The main checkout (or, under `worktree-always`, the scratch worktree the resolution runs in) is not any run's assigned worktree, so E1 denies unless the caller's ownership classifies as `foreign`, and the reconciling session usually owns the sibling runs. The procedure therefore closes this branch's run, then each other reconciliation branch's run E1 names in turn, and re-protects each one when the resolution lands or is abandoned.

That bullet drew #3809's whole-branch review Important 1, part of fix round 1, and four `/review` findings (3c at `:126` reproduced, plus single-agent 3b `:126`, 3c `:139`, 3f `:138`). The prose is correct today but is the most fragile part of the procedure, and it exists only because E1 cannot tell that a commit is concluding a merge of a live run's branch. E1's own deny message already names that case as legitimate ("If this checkout is intentionally correct (e.g. finishing the branch), clear the assignment first").

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a live-query exemption to E1, of the same shape as `isIntegrationBranchFastForwardPush` (#2542): a `commit` target is allowed when its checkout has a merge in progress (a `MERGE_HEAD` exists) **and** every commit `MERGE_HEAD` lists equals the current `HEAD` of a live run's worktree (`ctx.runState.worktree` or any entry in E1's existing `otherWorktrees` map). Log a new `wd-merge-finish` event (expected, actual, merged run dir) to `ctx.runDir` and allow.
- [ ] Every unprovable answer keeps today's E1 verdict (no exemption): no readable `MERGE_HEAD`, a `MERGE_HEAD` commit matching no live run's worktree `HEAD`, a run worktree whose `HEAD` cannot be read (removed worktree, git failure, timeout), or a target action other than `commit`
- [ ] Simplify `worktree-merge.md` step 5's Resolve-now bullet: drop the E1 chase (closing and re-protecting other reconciliation branches' runs) and keep the per-branch close-run ordering #3809 pinned (this branch's run closed first, re-protected after a step 4 failure)
- [ ] Document the exemption in `docs/hooks.md` beside E1's posture bullets

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`, a `git commit` in a checkout whose `MERGE_HEAD` equals a live sibling run's worktree `HEAD` is allowed and logs `wd-merge-finish`, while `ctx.runDir` names a different (newer) run
- The same commit is still denied when `MERGE_HEAD` is absent, when it names a commit that is no live run's worktree `HEAD`, when one of several `MERGE_HEAD` lines matches no live run, and when the matching run's worktree `HEAD` cannot be read. Each is its own test case.
- A `git push` or non-commit action is unaffected by the exemption
- Each new allow test goes red when the exemption is reverted (`git checkout --` on `pre-tool-use.js` only)
- `worktree-merge.md`'s Resolve-now bullet no longer instructs closing or re-protecting other branches' runs, and the existing #3809 ordering pins still pass
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Resolving a merge conflict during a multi-run local-merge reconciliation no longer has to close other branches' runs first.

## Technical Approach

The decision between the three signals the original request listed:

- **A run-state marker set and cleared by the reconciliation** was rejected. It adds a lifecycle (set before the merge, cleared on land or abandon) that the chase itself shows is fragile, and a marker left behind by a crash is a standing allow for that run's commits in the wrong checkout.
- **Narrowing E1's owner-unfiltered newest-run resolution in the main checkout** was rejected. The reconciling session usually owns the runs it merges, so their ownership verdict is `'mine'` and E1 would still deny. Narrowing further would also loosen E1 for the wrong-checkout commit it exists to catch.
- **A `MERGE_HEAD`-keyed live query** was chosen. Git already records the fact E1 lacks: a merge commit in progress whose parent-to-be is a live run's branch tip is that branch being integrated, not that run's work landing in the wrong checkout. It needs no new state, cannot go stale (git removes `MERGE_HEAD` when the merge concludes or aborts), and covers the `worktree-always` path too, where the resolution commits inside a scratch worktree that no run is assigned to.

Implementation follows `.claude/skills/pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions`: read `MERGE_HEAD` via `git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD` in the target's toplevel (a linked worktree's git dir differs from the main checkout's), compare commit ids exactly, read each candidate worktree's `HEAD` with `git -C {worktree} rev-parse HEAD`, resolve paths through `canonicalRealpath`, and fail closed on every inconclusive read.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — E1 tail loop in `runInner`: the `MERGE_HEAD` live-query exemption and `wd-merge-finish` event
- `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` — step 5 Resolve-now bullet: drop the E1 chase
- `docs/hooks.md` — E1 posture bullets
- `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` — allow and fail-closed cases
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `appendEvent` (no change expected)

## Gotchas

- The exemption must sit after the `otherWorktrees` check and before the `foreign`-ownership branch. That way it never reclassifies a commit already allowed as `wd-ambiguous`, and a `foreign` caller keeps its existing allow + `systemMessage`.
- Under `worktree-always`, the fast-forward of the main checkout is `git merge --ff-only`, which is not a `commit` target, so only the scratch-worktree commit needs the exemption. Confirm with `gitTargetsFrom` before assuming otherwise.
- An octopus merge lists several commits in `MERGE_HEAD`; require every line to match, so a merge that also pulls in an unrelated branch keeps today's deny.
- The `worktree-merge.md` bullet is pinned by #3809's conformance tests; keep "this branch's run is closed first" and the step 4 re-protection wording intact.

## Original request

Let E1 allow a multi-run reconciliation's conflict-resolution commit without closing sibling runs

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3809

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's **Resolve now** bullet carries a multi-run chase: the conflict resolution ends in a commit in the main checkout, which the working-directory hook (E1, `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`) checks against the newest non-terminal run in the project regardless of owner (`plugin/bin/hooks.js` resolveRunDir, owner-unfiltered). So before the commit can land, the procedure closes this branch's run, then every other reconciliation branch's run E1 names in turn, and must re-protect each one when the resolution lands or is abandoned.

That one bullet drew #3809's whole-branch review Important 1, part of fix round 1, and four /review findings (3c at :126 reproduced, plus single-agent 3b :126, 3c :139, 3f :138). The prose workaround is correct now but is the most fragile part of the procedure, and it exists only because E1 cannot tell that a main-checkout commit belongs to a human-present reconciliation.

## Deliverables

Decide how E1 should treat a commit in the main checkout made while reconciling several runs' branches — so the reconciliation does not have to close sibling runs to get its resolution commit through — and implement that decision in the hook.

Then simplify `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's Resolve-now bullet to drop the E1 chase, keeping the per-branch close-run ordering #3809 pinned.

## Open Question

Which signal should let E1 allow this commit without closing other runs: a run-state marker that the reconciliation sets (and clears) on each run it is merging, a reconciliation-scoped exemption keyed on MERGE_HEAD naming a branch whose run is in the reconciliation, or narrowing E1's owner-unfiltered newest-run resolution for the main checkout? Each changes the never-break-a-session posture in docs/hooks.md differently.

## Release Note

Resolving a merge conflict during a multi-run local-merge reconciliation no longer has to close other branches' runs first.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — E1 decision for a reconciliation commit in the main checkout
- `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` — drop step 5's E1 chase

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (which runs a MERGE_HEAD line may match): Reading A — keep the live-only candidate set exactly as Deliverables 1-2 and the second Acceptance Criterion say (`ctx.runState.worktree` or an `otherWorktrees` entry; a `status: clean` run's `worktreeAtClose` never counts). Amend Deliverable 3: Resolve now no longer closes this branch's run before the resolution commit. The run stays live (it was never closed after a step-2 predicted conflict, and it was re-protected after a step-4 failure), so the exemption matches its worktree HEAD. Run step 3's close-run fence for that run only once the resolution lands (after `git commit --no-edit --cleanup=strip`, or after the `worktree-always` fast-forward). An abandoned resolution therefore has no run closed for it. Keep the step 3 fence order and the AC3 phrases in `tests/local-merge-close-run-ordering.test.js` passing. No test pins the "closed first" wording, so the Gotcha that says to keep it no longer applies.
- Q2 (run-less reconciliation branch): drop the E1 chase entirely (Deliverable 3). If E1 still denies the resolution commit of a branch that has no run, run `git merge --abort`, report the deny, and handle the branch as **Skip this branch**: merge the remaining branches first (each run is closed at step 3 as its branch merges), then return to this branch from step 1. If E1 still denies on the return, treat the resolution as abandoned and report the run E1 named. No other branch's run is closed or re-protected to get the commit through.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

Origin: reflect (light mode, Friction lens) from #3675's wrap-up run (2026-10-20T162315-record-3675).
**Related:** #3690 (absorbed), #3188, #3295, #3737, #3740, #3812, #3898, #3956, #3963

## Current State

In #3675's dispatch group, both dispatched Task calls — `build,test` and `review,polish,wrap-up` — found mid-run that no `Agent`/`Task` tool was available, ran their work inline, and each self-reported the gap in `decisions.md` as a `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` deviation. Nothing defective shipped, but the same discovery happened twice in one run.

Since then, half of this is settled. #3078 (`364762254`) gave `_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Foreground Execution Discipline a **Fallback** for "no `Agent`/`Task` tool exists (`ToolSearch` finds none, deferred or otherwise — the normal case in a cloud routine sandbox)", restated in `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s Context pack item 7: judge the unit in-session, log the downgrade, mark its findings `unconfirmed`. That covers read-only units (lenses, single reads, judges) — the review call's side.

The build side is still uncovered, and two rules now contradict each other there:

- The Fallback is explicitly limited to read-only units; for a write-capable child it says only that one still silent at the bound is never redone in-session (because an abandoned child keeps running and may still write).
- `build/execution-mode-policy.md` (#491) rules that executing the plan's substance directly in-session, skipping Task dispatch, is **never licensed** — under a locked `execution-strategy: subagent-only` or otherwise.

The same environment has already produced two different outcomes. In run `2026-10-20T022848-record-3630` (record #3630, filed as #3690, absorbed here), the dispatched build stopped at `/build`'s Common Step 2 before any implementation (#3690's report calls it a HARD-GATE; `build/SKILL.md` has no gate by that literal name there, so the stop presumably came from the call honoring `execution-mode-policy.md`'s never-licensed rule), and Settle classified it `transient` and kept `auto:build`, so every retry in that sandbox would stop the same way. In #3675's run, the build ran inline instead and reported a concern.

So a dispatched `build,test` call under `execution-strategy: subagent-only` that has no `Agent` tool has no compliant path: `/superpowers:subagent-driven-development` cannot dispatch implementers, inline execution is forbidden, and nothing says to stop. #3675's call improvised inline execution and reported it as a concern. Nothing about this case is anomalous — the core file itself calls it the normal case in a cloud routine sandbox — yet each call discovers it mid-run, after the plan is written.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Foreground Execution Discipline names the **no-nested-agent environment** once, as an expected environment class, and distinguishes its two cases: a child abandoned at the bound (today's rule — a write-capable one is never redone in-session) versus a child that was **never launched because no `Agent` tool exists** (no child exists, so nothing can still be writing, and the unit — write-capable or not — is done in-session)
- [ ] `build/execution-mode-policy.md` gains one carve-out to #491's "never licensed": a dispatched Task call (not the interactive orchestrating session) that has no `Agent` tool executes the plan in-session. State why this keeps #491's rationale: the dispatched call is already a clean room separate from the session that dispatched it, and the second Task call (`review,polish,wrap-up`) remains a separate agent, so the review is still independent of the code's author
- [ ] `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s first-call (`build,test`) template tells the call to probe for the `Agent` tool once, **before** choosing an execution strategy (one `ToolSearch`), and on no tool to take the carve-out from the start instead of discovering it mid-plan; Context pack item 7 carries the same distinction for any dispatch that writes
- [ ] The downgrade logs as one canonical `decisions.md` `AUTO` entry (per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s schema) naming the environment — e.g. `no nested Agent tool — plan executed in-session` — and the call returns `STATUS: DONE`, not `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS`, when that was the only deviation
- [ ] The read-only Fallback keeps its `unconfirmed` marking unchanged — a self-judged lens finding is still weaker evidence than a second reader's

## Acceptance Criteria

- `subagent-dispatch-core.md` states that a write-capable unit whose child was never launched (no `Agent` tool) is executed in-session, and that a write-capable child abandoned at the bound still ends `STATUS: BLOCKED` — both rules present, and distinguishable by whether a child was ever launched
- `build/execution-mode-policy.md` names the dispatched-call-with-no-`Agent`-tool carve-out and still states that the interactive orchestrating session may never execute the plan directly
- `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s `build,test` template contains the up-front probe instruction, ordered before the execution-strategy choice
- `tests/foreground-execution-instruction.test.js` (or the suite that pins these sections) asserts the new never-launched-vs-abandoned distinction in the core section, item 7, and the build template, and reverting the core-file sentence turns it red
- The canonical `AUTO` line's wording is pinned in one place and cited, not restated, by the template
- A `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` firing against a `subagent-only` record, in an environment whose dispatched Task call has no `Agent` tool, builds via the carve-out rather than stopping at Common Step 2 or being settled `transient` (the #3690 failure)
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Dispatched builds in sandboxes without nested agents now follow a defined path instead of improvising and flagging a concern.

## Technical Approach

The key distinction is whether a child was ever launched. The existing "never redo a write-capable child in-session" rule exists because an abandoned child keeps running and may still write (`subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Fallback). With no `Agent` tool there is no child, so that hazard cannot occur, and in-session execution of a write-capable unit is safe. Write that reasoning into the core file once, and have `task-prompt.md` item 7 and the `build,test` template restate the rule (they are inlined verbatim into a `Task()` prompt whose agent never reads the core file — `docs/skill-graph.md`'s `subagent-dispatch-core.md` row).

The probe is one `ToolSearch` for the `Agent` tool at the start of the `build,test` call. A probe by the top-level dispatcher would not work: the dispatcher has a Task tool by construction (it is dispatching), and whether its children get a nested one depends on the environment and Claude Code version (`subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Background-work paragraph, #3722's measurements).

#491's carve-out is narrow on purpose: it licenses in-session execution only for a dispatched Task call that has no `Agent` tool. An interactive session that has the tool and chooses not to use it is still non-compliant.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md` — Foreground Execution Discipline: name the environment class; never-launched vs abandoned
- `plugin/skills/build/execution-mode-policy.md` — the dispatched-call carve-out to #491
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` — Context pack item 7 and the `build,test` template's up-front probe
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md` — only if the canonical entry needs a new reason slug
- `tests/foreground-execution-instruction.test.js` — pins the core section, item 7, and both templates
- `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` — check for pinned Fallback wording
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — the `subagent-dispatch-core.md` edge row describing what item 7 restates

## Gotchas

- `/flow`'s `multispec-parallel-waves.md` inlines item 7 and the `build,test` clause verbatim (`docs/skill-graph.md`), so changing either changes what parallel-wave members receive — update that file in the same change.
- `tests/foreground-execution-instruction.test.js` pins the core section, item 7, and both templates against each other; edit all four together or it goes red.
- The decision is about the dispatched Task call, not `/superpowers:subagent-driven-development` itself (an upstream skill this repo does not edit) — the carve-out tells the call to execute the plan in-session in place of invoking that skill.
- #3188 (open) proposes mechanical enforcement of `execution-strategy: subagent-only` (a PreToolUse check or a `/build` Step 2 assertion). Whatever it lands must honor this carve-out — a dispatched call with no `Agent` tool executing in-session is compliant, not a violation.
- `/build`'s Common Step 2 is where #3630's build stopped; the carve-out has to be reachable from there (the probe result decides the execution strategy before Common Step 2 resolves it), or the build stops anyway.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: #3675's two calls lacked the tool because of the environment (cloud sandbox or a headless Claude Code version), not a one-off harness fault — the run's `decisions.md` was not preserved in the archive, so confirm the class by checking `subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Background-work measurements against the run's environment if it can be identified.

## Original request

Dispatch contract doesn't name or detect an Agent/Task-tool-less sandbox

Origin: reflect (light mode, Friction lens) from #3675's wrap-up run (2026-10-20T162315-record-3675).
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s subagent contract, and `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`'s
two-call gate, assume `execution-strategy: subagent-only` dispatched Task calls have the
Agent/Task tool available for nested fan-out. In this run's dispatch group (record #3675), both
dispatched calls — `build,test` and `review,polish,wrap-up` — independently discovered mid-run
that no Agent/Task tool was available, and both fell back to running their work inline, each
self-reporting the gap in `decisions.md` as a `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` deviation. Both degraded
gracefully and no defect landed in the shipped work, but the gap recurred identically across two
independent calls in the same run rather than being a one-off anomaly.

## Open Question

Should the dispatch contract (or dispatch's own two-call gate) detect Agent/Task-tool absence up
front — either declaring the limitation inline in the dispatch prompt's own preamble, or treating
a Task-tool-less sandbox as a named, expected environment class — rather than leaving each
dispatched call to discover and self-report the gap independently every time? Or is the existing
per-call self-report-and-degrade pattern (DONE_WITH_CONCERNS + a decisions.md note) sufficient as
is, given it already surfaces the gap without blocking?

## Release Note

n/a — no code change proposed yet; this issue exists to get a maintainer decision on whether one
is warranted.

Surface: infra

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3664, ledger rows 3-4)
**Related:** #3664, #3646, #3792, #3942

## Current State

The ephemeral dev server a pipeline starts (`_shared/dev-url-detection.md`'s Ephemeral server start, items 3-4) is recorded as one line, `{pid} {port} {worktree-root} detached:{yes|no}`, in `ephemeral-server.txt`. POSIX launches under `setsid` and records `detached:yes`; Windows has no detach primitive and records `detached:no` (`dev-url-detection.md:130-131`). The recorded pid is the shell leader; the listening socket can belong to its child.

Every stop identifies the server only by that pid and port. `wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section D (#3664) validates the record's shape and keeps it when the port is still held after the kill, but proves neither identity:

- **Kill side (step 2):** any positive-integer pid is signalled (`kill {pid}`, plus `kill -- -{pid}` under `detached:yes`; `taskkill /PID {pid} /T /F` on win32). A pid reused by an unrelated process after the server died gets killed, along with its tree on win32.
- **Port side (step 4):** a port still held after an "already stopped" pid is reported as the server's survivor, though the holder may be an unrelated process.

A "pid listens on port" probe does not settle it, because the listener is usually the leader's child, and after the leader dies a non-detached child is reparented, so a parent-chain walk breaks.

The same stop logic is restated as agent-read prose in other places: `review/step3-routing.md`'s fix-wave server coordination (around line 124), `_shared/dev-url-detection.md`'s standalone stop, `flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s shared teardown (line 176), and `flow/multispec-parallel-waves.md`'s per-member stop (line 54). Each guard is pinned by text, not by behavior.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Identity rule:** a process is identified by `(pid, start time)`. When the server starts, capture two identities: the **leader** (the pid recorded today) and the **listener** (the process holding the port once the readiness poll in item 3 succeeds). Write both, with start times, to a sidecar `ephemeral-server.json` beside `ephemeral-server.txt`. The txt line keeps its format, since `detached:` is parsed as its last token.
- [ ] **Kill side:** signal a recorded process only when its current start time matches the recorded one; a mismatch or a missing pid is "already stopped". Under `detached:yes`, the group kill stays keyed on the verified leader.
- [ ] **Port side:** after the kill, a port holder is the server's survivor only when it matches the recorded listener identity, or (under `detached:yes`) its process group is the recorded leader's. Any other holder is reported as "port {port} held by unrelated pid {x}", and the record is deleted, since the recorded server is gone.
- [ ] **One executable helper:** add a `plugin/bin/` CLI (e.g. `dev-server.js` with `record` and `stop` verbs, using the injectable-runner seam in `.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern`'s CLI wrapper contract). Every prose site above calls it instead of restating the stop: the Ephemeral server start's item 4 (record), Section D, `step3-routing.md`, the standalone stop, and both `/flow` multi-spec teardown sites (stop).
- [ ] **Legacy records:** a run whose record has no sidecar (started before this change) keeps today's behavior, logged once as `identity unverified (legacy record)`. Give that branch a removal condition per this repo's deprecation rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests with a fake process table: a recorded pid whose start time differs is not signalled and reports already stopped; a matching one is signalled; a port held by the recorded listener (alive after a leader-only stop) is reported as the survivor and the record is kept; a port held by an unrelated process is reported as unrelated and the record is deleted; a `detached:yes` child in the leader's process group counts as the survivor
- Each of those tests goes red against a helper that skips the identity check
- A conformance test asserts that none of the stop sites restate `kill {pid}` / `taskkill /PID` / an `lsof … | xargs kill` stop inline and that each one calls the helper
- A live probe on macOS (and Linux in CI where available) starts a real `setsid` shell-leader server, records it, and stops it through the helper, with the leader and listener identities matching what `ps` reports
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Pipeline cleanup no longer signals a process that merely reused a dead dev server's pid, and no longer blames an unrelated process for a port it failed to free.

## Technical Approach

The two candidate rules in the original question were a pid-listens-on-port probe (it fails for the shell-leader/child shape, as the record notes) and some stronger identity. Start time is the standard way to tell a reused pid from the original. POSIX: `ps -o lstart= -p {pid}` or `ps -o etimes=`; win32: `Win32_Process.CreationDate` via PowerShell `Get-CimInstance`. A reused pid cannot share its predecessor's start time. Capturing the listener's own identity at start, instead of deriving it from the leader at stop, sidesteps the reparenting problem entirely.

Listener lookup at record time: POSIX `lsof -nP -iTCP:{port} -sTCP:LISTEN -t`, with `ss -ltnp` as a fallback where `lsof` is absent; win32 `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort {port} -State Listen` → `OwningProcess`.

Fail direction: an identity the helper cannot read (no `ps`, a CIM failure) is unprovable, so it signals nothing and reports a cleanup failure, keeping the record. A leaked dev server is recoverable; a killed unrelated process is not.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/dev-server.js` — new CLI: `record` and `stop` verbs
- `plugin/bin/lib/dev-server/` — new module: identity capture, verify, stop (injectable runner)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — Ephemeral server start item 4 (record via helper), standalone stop
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — Section D steps 2-4 call the helper
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — fix-wave server coordination
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md` — shared teardown step 1
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-parallel-waves.md` — per-member server stop
- `tests/bin-lib/dev-server/` — unit tests with a fake process table
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — list the new CLI and module

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: `ps -o lstart=` and `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` return a start time stable enough to compare exactly (second resolution) on the CI runners; if `etimes` is used instead, compare with a small tolerance and test the boundary.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: once the readiness poll succeeds, the listener is already bound and visible to `lsof`/`ss`/`Get-NetTCPConnection` without elevated privileges on macOS, Linux CI, and win32 CI. The original record noted no probe had been run against a real `detached:no` / `detached:yes` leader — run one before relying on it.
- The `bin/` CLIs must not read `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` at runtime (unset in Bash); follow the existing CLIs' process-cwd anchoring.
- `multispec-parallel-waves.md`'s members may start servers without a run-dir sidecar path; check where each member writes its record before wiring the helper.

## Original request

wrap-up Section D never proves the recorded pid or port belongs to the server it recorded

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3664, ledger rows 3-4)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

wrap-up Section D (`plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md`) identifies the dev server it stops only by the pid and port in `ephemeral-server.txt`. #3664 made it validate the record's shape (four fields, positive-integer pid and port, a `detached:` token) and keep the record when the port is still held after the kill, but nothing proves the recorded pid is still the server it was recorded for. Kill side: step 2 signals any positive-integer pid, so a pid reused by an unrelated process after the server died is signalled. Port side: step 4 reports a port still held after an "already stopped" pid as the survivor, though the holder may be an unrelated process. A pid-listens-on-port probe does not settle it: a `detached:no` or `detached:yes` record names the shell leader, and the listening socket belongs to its child. The stop logic is also agent-read prose in three places (Section D, review's fix-wave server coordination in `step3-routing.md`, and the standalone stop in `_shared/dev-url-detection.md`), so each guard is pinned by text, not by behavior. Refs #3664 (its review ledger rows 3-4).

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide the identity rule: how the recorded server is told from an unrelated process on the recorded pid (kill side) and on the recorded port (port side), covering the shell-leader and child-socket record shapes on POSIX and win32.
- [ ] Apply the rule in every place that stops a recorded dev server, preferably through one executable stop helper the three prose sites call, so the rule is tested by behavior.
- [ ] Pin it with a test that fails against the current text.

## Open Question

Which identity check is sound for the shell-leader and child-socket shapes `ephemeral-server.txt` legitimately records, and is a single executable stop helper the right home for it? Insufficient evidence: no probe has been tried against a real `detached:no` / `detached:yes` leader.

## Release Note

Pipeline cleanup no longer signals a process that merely reused a dead dev server's pid, and no longer blames an unrelated process for a port it failed to free.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — modify

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (standalone stop): Reading A — outside a pipeline, the Ephemeral server start also calls `dev-server.js record`, which writes the same `ephemeral-server.txt` line and `ephemeral-server.json` sidecar into a per-server directory `dev-server-{port}/` under the session temp root (`_shared/session-tmp-root.md`'s `sessionTmpPath($CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, …)`, falling back to unscoped `os.tmpdir()` when there is no session id). The standalone stop calls `dev-server.js stop` on that directory. `record` and `stop` accept that directory under the anchored-or-outside rule: they refuse a path inside any checkout that is not anchored under the main checkout, and accept a path outside every checkout. They append no `decisions.md` entry on this path.
- Q2 (go-red criterion): Reading A — keep the criterion as written: all five fake-process-table tests must fail against a helper that skips the identity check. Each positive scenario (matching leader signalled, recorded listener survivor, `detached:yes` group-child survivor) also puts a reused-pid process with a different start time in the table, and asserts it is neither signalled nor reported as the survivor. The unrelated-holder test also asserts that nothing is signalled. The build proves each red by running the five tests against an identity-skipping mutant.
